BLND.name: Blend Labs, Inc.
BLND.fact: Blend is a fintech company that aims to use software to simplify the process of getting loans, opening deposit accounts, and more. It also partners with financial service providers to help grow and nurture customers.

LAMR.name: Lamar Advertising Company
LAMR.fact: Figaro! Figaro! Opera has a special place in the history of Lamar Advertising. In 1902, it was known as the "Pensacola Advertising Company" and was focused on posters promoting the Pensacola Opera House.

AMP.name: Ameriprise Financial, Inc.
AMP.fact: Ameriprise achieved a personal record for assets under management and administration at 973 billion.

ETR.name: Entergy Corporation
ETR.fact: Founder Harvey C. Couch used sawdust from a lumber company to bring electricity to rural Arkansas.

ABBV.name: AbbVie Inc.
ABBV.fact: Humira accounted for over half of 2018 revenues.

PFG.name: Principal Financial Group, Inc.
PFG.fact: In 1925, Principal Financial Group acquired a small, 500-watt radio station, WHO, with a broadcast range of 150 miles. George Kuhns saw this tool as a way to increase sales.

LAZ.name: Lazard Inc
LAZ.fact: Five French brothers, and several cousins, emigrated to the United States of America and started a company in 1848. The relatives formed "Lazard Freres," meaning Lazard Brothers and the family business sold dry goods in New Orleans. A few years later, the brothers ventured into the world of banking and the rest is history.

EXPO.name: Exponent, Inc.
EXPO.fact: Three professors from Stanford University, and several engineers from Stanford Research Institute, founded the company with only $500 in capital.

TRIP.name: Tripadvisor, Inc.
TRIP.fact: TripAdvisor is the world's largest travel guidance platform - available in 43 markets and 22 languages.

CBU.name: Community Bank System, Inc.
CBU.fact: Community Bank System's roots go back to 1866. With over 150 years of experience, the bank has grown to 225+ branches, 3,000+ employees, and 650,000+ customers.

TDG.name: TransDigm Group Incorporated
TDG.fact: This company designs high-end aerospace components for commercial planes and the U.S. Military.

BOX.name: Box, Inc.
BOX.fact: As of 2022, Box had 97,000 companies as its customers, as well as 68% of the Fortune 500 using its services.

CE.name: Celanese Corporation
CE.fact: Celanese Acetate products are made from cellulose - a renewable, sustainable resource sourced from managed forests. Acetate yarns were initially developed as an alternative to silk.

PII.name: Polaris Inc.
PII.fact: The Polaris co-founders developed an early snowmobile in 1955. To prove the vehicles weren't just frivolous toys, Edgar and three friends embarked on a 1,200-mile journey across the Alaskan wilderness to demonstrate the vehicle's durability. The company has since expanded its product line into ATVs, military vehicles, boats, airplanes, and more.

RGLD.name: Royal Gold, Inc.
RGLD.fact: Royal Gold is one of the world's leading precious metal streams, but the company did not start there. In fact, the firm started as an oil-exploration company.

CUZ.name: Cousins Properties Incorporated
CUZ.fact: Thomas Cousins, founder of the present-day REIT, hired his dad as the first employee of the company.

NBIX.name: Neurocrine Biosciences, Inc.
NBIX.fact: This biopharmaceutical company develops treatments for Parkinson's disease, Tourette syndrome, and congenital adrenal hyperplasia.

OHI.name: Omega Healthcare Investors, Inc.
OHI.fact: Through 2021, Omega ranked 2nd among healthcare REITs and 50th in total shareholder return among all REITs.

SMPL.name: The Simply Good Foods Company
SMPL.fact: The Simply Good Food Company owns the famous health brands Atkins and Quest.

NVDA.name: NVIDIA Corporation
NVDA.fact: NVIDIA has developed Drive PX 2, a platform for self-driving cars, and is partnering with a growing number of automakers, including Tesla, to integrate and advance the technology.

MGNX.name: MacroGenics, Inc.
MGNX.fact: MacroGenics is developing monoclonal antibody-based treatments for cancer. It is best known for "Margenza", an injectable used in combination with chemotherapy to fight metastatic breast cancer.

IT.name: Gartner, Inc.
IT.fact: This company has posted 35 consecutive quarters of double-digit growth.

MDU.name: MDU Resources Group, Inc.
MDU.fact: MDU is proud to be the largest publicly traded company headquartered in North Dakota. As of 2022, the company has paid dividends uninterrupted to its shareholders for 84 years. MDU values its roots and heritage so much that they have kept the same symbol (MDU) on the NYSE since 1948.

TWLO.name: Twilio Inc.
TWLO.fact: Twilio has 26 offices in 17 countries, spanning 5 continents. The company offers highly scalable communications and customer engagement solutions, with over 20,000 companies currently using its Segment platform. Twilio solutions include AI that seeks to optimize interactions at each level of engagement.

VMI.name: Valmont Industries, Inc.
VMI.fact: A strong man with a brilliant vision invested his entire life savings  ($5,000) into a company that he believed in. Robert Daugherty laid the foundation for what would later become a leader in infrastructure and agriculture. Today, Valmont is located on six continents and serves more than 100 countries.

PAYC.name: Paycom Software, Inc.
PAYC.fact: Paycom was recently added to the S&P 500 in January 2019. Since then, they were ranked sixth on Fortune's 100 Fastest Growing Companies List which takes into account revenues, profits, and stock returns.

ICE.name: Intercontinental Exchange, Inc.
ICE.fact: If you want to "go public" and offer shares on the New York Stock Exchange, it'll cost you. Intercontinental Exchange requires an initial application fee of $25,000 and, when you finally list shares, a one-time special charge of $50,000. The issuer must also pay a per-share fee of $0.004, subject to a maximum of $295,000.

CB.name: Chubb Limited
CB.fact: The origins of the Chubb Corporation date back to 1882 when Thomas Caldecot Chubb and his son Percy opened their marine underwriting business in the seaport district of New York City. Having collected $1,000 from each of 100 prominent merchants to start their venture, they focused initially on insuring ships and cargoes.

HCA.name: HCA Healthcare, Inc.
HCA.fact: The HCA Foundation has partnered with HCA and the Nashville Technology Council (NTC) to bring together Nashville's best visual designers and software developers  including many HCA team members - to work collaboratively to build technology solutions for local nonprofits.

AAP.name: Advance Auto Parts, Inc.
AAP.fact: One of the original names of Advanced Auto Parts was Pep Boys. The name was created by the founders in 1921.

SSD.name: Simpson Manufacturing Co., Inc.
SSD.fact: With seven accredited state-of-the-art test labs, Simpson has supported 98% of the top 100 builders.

UPWK.name: Upwork Inc.
UPWK.fact: In March 2022, TIME's List of 100 Most Influential Companies included Upwork for the innovative and important work that has been done.

EYE.name: National Vision Holdings, Inc.
EYE.fact: National Vision owns several iconic vision brands including, AC Lens, Vista Optical, and Vision Center (the Walmart brand).

GHM.name: Graham Corporation
GHM.fact: Vacuum and heat transfer equipment - Graham is known for providing precision equipment to the energy industry and process manufacturers.

FCF.name: First Commonwealth Financial Corporation
FCF.fact: First Commonwealth's headquarters is located in Indiana, Pennsylvania - "The Christmas Tree Capital of the World" - just a few blocks from the Jimmy Stewart Museum. The bank did not need a bailout during the financial crisis of 2008-09, due to its excellent financial strength.

BC.name: Brunswick Corporation
BC.fact: John Brunswick founded the company in 1845 with the intention of the business being the production of carriages. Soon after opening his shop, he decided that making billiards tables would be more lucrative. Over the years, the company diversified into toilet seats, automobile tires, target-drone aircraft, school furniture, and many other very unrelated products. Brunswick has since focused on its many boating brands such as Mercury, Mastervolt, Princecraft, and many more.

INCY.name: Incyte Corporation
INCY.fact: As of 2014, this company was developing baricitinib, an oralJAK1 and JAK2 inhibitor drug for rheumatoid arthritis in partnership with Eli Lilly.

BFAM.name: Bright Horizons Family Solutions Inc.
BFAM.fact: In 1986, the Co-founder's home was used as Bright Horizons headquarters in its infant stages. The company has thus grown to be the largest provider of employer-sponsored child care.

UCB.name: United Community Banks, Inc.
UCB.fact: Emmanuel Janssen founded UCB in 1928 with an initial focus on industrial chemicals and was one of the first companies to distill ammonia from coal.

ZION.name: Zions Bancorporation, National Association
ZION.fact: During the Panic of 1893, the bank managed not only to remain solvent but actually continued to grow.

HR.name: Healthcare Realty Trust Incorporated
HR.fact: From an initial portfolio of 21 healthcare facilities, Healthcare Realty owns 258 properties and as of 2022, owns 17.9 million square feet of space.

PNFP.name: Pinnacle Financial Partners, Inc.
PNFP.fact: This financial services company gained naming rights for a new skyscraper in Downtown Nashville, electing to call the 29-story and 65,000-square feet building the Pinnacle at Symphony Place.

BRKR.name: Bruker Corporation
BRKR.fact: Bruker was incorporated in 1960 and located in the backyard of a Karlsruhe residence.

AMN.name: AMN Healthcare Services, Inc.
AMN.fact: Carlon is derived from the word "care" and the suffix "-lon," which means full and complete. The name adequately represents the goal of the company: a commitment to complete care.

ORLY.name: O'Reilly Automotive, Inc.
ORLY.fact: O'Reilly Automotive was founded by the descendants of Michael Byrne O'Reilly, an Irishman who fled the Irish Potato Famine in 1849.

CHCO.name: City Holding Company
CHCO.fact: Parent company of several banks, City Holding operates primarily in West Virgina, Ohio, and California. Assets totaled near $6 billion as of 2021.

SIBN.name: SI-BONE, Inc.
SIBN.fact: SI-BONE pioneered minimally invasive sacroliac joint fusion surgery, which helps people around the world find relief from chronic lower back pain. The company's proprietary tech is called the iFuse Implant System

AJG.name: Arthur J. Gallagher & Co.
AJG.fact: In 1938, Arthur Gallagher helped create The Hartford Groups groundbreaking Retrospective Rating Program, which rewarded customers who minimized their losses.

BHF.name: Brighthouse Financial, Inc.
BHF.fact: With over 2 million customers, Brighthouse Financial ranked #353 on Fortune 500 List in 2021.

PENN.name: PENN Entertainment, Inc.
PENN.fact: Penn National Gaming operates approx. 40 casino gaming and racing facilities in the U.S. and Canada, under the Hollywood brand. The company also owns a 36% stake in Barstool Sports.

IART.name: Integra LifeSciences Holdings Corporation
IART.fact: Integra was the first company to commercially reproduce skin tissue used to treat severe burns and other skin issues.

LOB.name: Live Oak Bancshares, Inc.
LOB.fact: In 2020, Live Oak Bancshares was the leading Small Business Administration and USDA lender by dollar volume.

A.name: Agilent Technologies, Inc.
A.fact: Agilent Technologies conducts cancer research. The oldest direct fossil evidence of cancer may be the leg bone of a shell-less proto-turtle.

NFE.name: New Fortress Energy Inc.
NFE.fact: Wes Edens was dedicated to reducing carbon emissions and fostering economic development through universal access to cleaner, affordable, and reliable energy. So, Wes decided to do something about it in 2014 when he founded New Fortress. The work of his company has improved the lives of millions through its liquefied natural gas (LNG) terminals, power generation facilities, and logistics assets across the world.

GXO.name: GXO Logistics, Inc.
GXO.fact: The multinational logistics company has approximately 900 warehouse locations and roughly 200 million square feet of warehouse space across 28 countries.

ALB.name: Albemarle Corporation
ALB.fact: In late November of 2020, the world's top lithium producer Albemarle joined forces with 27 companies, including electric vehicles maker Tesla and ride share company Uber, to form a group that is pushing for 100% electric vehicle sales in the US by 2030.

VRTX.name: Vertex Pharmaceuticals Incorporated
VRTX.fact: Vertex has received numerous awards over the years including making Fast Company's list of World's 50 Most Innovative Companies in 2020 and scoring a perfect rating on the Human Rights Campaign's 2020 Corporate Equality Index.

BOOT.name: Boot Barn Holdings, Inc.
BOOT.fact: A leader in western and work-related footwear and apparel, Boot Barn also owns the brands Wrangler, Ariat, Cinch, Idyllwind, and Lucchese Boots.

SHC.name: Sotera Health Company
SHC.fact: The name Sotera Health was inspired by Soteria, the Greek goddess of safety, and reflects the Company’s unwavering commitment to its mission.

FNKO.name: Funko, Inc.
FNKO.fact: Funko was founded in 1988 by toy collector, Mike Becker, who was frustrated when he could not find an affordable coin bank of the "Big Boy" restaurant mascot. Becker secured licensing rights and started making his own. Funko would later sell 80,000 Big Boy bobbleheads following the "Austin Powers" movie.

SRE.name: Sempra
SRE.fact: Sempra Energy works on building clean transportation infrastructure. They have installed more than 3,000 electric vehicle charging stations at nearly 255 locations in their service territory.

LII.name: Lennox International Inc.
LII.fact: Dave Lennox, Founder of Lennox, built the industry's first riveted-steel furnace.

QGEN.name: Qiagen N.V.
QGEN.fact: Qiagen is a worldwide brand and the company's current portfolio covers more than 500 products.

CACI.name: CACI International Inc
CACI.fact: This IT company has roughly 23,000 employees.

FANG.name: Diamondback Energy, Inc.
FANG.fact: Diamondback Energy uses horizontal drilling to reduce surface use and impact. It also increases production rate by increasing the ratio of wellbore length exposed to the "pay zone".

DAR.name: Darling Ingredients Inc.
DAR.fact: Darling Ingredients traces its origins back to 1882. Lucius Darling owned a slaughterhouse and developed new ways to use every part of the animal, which had otherwise gone to waste. His ingenuity led the company we know today.

CINF.name: Cincinnati Financial Corporation
CINF.fact: The Cincinnati Insurance Company was founded nearly 70 years ago by four independent insurance agents.

MDLZ.name: Mondelez International, Inc.
MDLZ.fact: On June 30, 2016, Mondelez made a $23 billion offer to buy its smaller rival, Hershey. The half-cash, half-stock deal valued Hershey stock at $107 a share. Hershey's board, however, unanimously rejected the offer.

ALK.name: Alaska Air Group, Inc.
ALK.fact: Contrary to popular belief, Alaska Airlines is headquartered in Seattle, Washington.

SAFE.name: Safehold Inc.
SAFE.fact: Over its first 25-years, Safehold completed $40 billion of transactions.

RSG.name: Republic Services, Inc.
RSG.fact: About 75% of its residential routes have been converted to automated single driver trucks.

BYND.name: Beyond Meat, Inc.
BYND.fact: Beyond Meat sells various plant-based options for several types of meat, hence the name "Beyond Meat." As of 2021, the plant-based products are available in roughly 118,000 food service and retail outlets across more than 80 countries.

MTB.name: M&T Bank Corporation
MTB.fact: In 2014, M&T Bank and the Baltimore Ravens announce a 10-year, $60 million extension of their partnership, which includes the continuation of naming rights to M&T Bank Stadium and an array of community-focused programs, including a new initiative focused on helping at-risk children in Baltimore.

HON.name: Honeywell International Inc.
HON.fact: When the company was named Minneapolis-Honeywell, they developed a tank periscope and camera stabilizers. They also built the C-1 autopilot. The C-1 revolutionized precision bombing in the war effort and was used on the  two B-29 bombers that dropped atomic bombs on Japan in 1945.

SHAK.name: Shake Shack Inc.
SHAK.fact: Shake Shack started as a hot dog cart inside Madison Square Park.

BRX.name: Brixmor Property Group Inc.
BRX.fact: This company is a REIT. Its largest tenants are TJX Companies, Kroger, Dollar Tree, Publix, Ross Stores, among others.

FTNT.name: Fortinet, Inc.
FTNT.fact: FortiVet is a program started by Fortinet designed to facilitate the transition of exceptional military veterans into the cyber-security industry, providing professional networking, training, and mentoring.

EWBC.name: East West Bancorp, Inc.
EWBC.fact: As of April 2019, East West Bancorp had $42.1 billion in assets. The company operates in over 120 locations worldwide with a primary focus on the United States of America and Chinese markets.

UBSI.name: United Bankshares, Inc.
UBSI.fact: The company traces its roots back to an eventful St. Patrick's Day in 1839 and since then they have had a tradition around that holiday. In 2022, United Bank celebrated its 183rd anniversary of giving out shamrocks to its customers.

GLOB.name: Globant S.A.
GLOB.fact: Globant was founded in Buenos Aires, Argentina, but the headquarters have since moved to Luxembourg.

SDGR.name: Schrödinger, Inc.
SDGR.fact: Schrodinger's chemical simulation software helps accelerate research into advanced chemistry, with the power of AI.

MORN.name: Morningstar, Inc.
MORN.fact: Morningstar was started in a one-bedroom apartment and the name Morningstar derives itself from the last sentence in Walden, Henry David Thoreau's book; "the sun is but a morning star."

WRB.name: W. R. Berkley Corporation
WRB.fact: W.R. Berkley Corp. is the creation of entrepreneur and investor William R. Berkley. Berkley got his start as an investor at the age of 12, when he began using spare money from his lawn-mowing business to buy stocks.

NTB.name: The Bank of N.T. Butterfield & Son Limited

TEL.name: TE Connectivity plc
TEL.fact: This company specializes in designing and manufacturing connectivity and sensor products for harsh environments. They manufacture for industries such as aerospace, medical, defense, and oil and gas.

CROX.name: Crocs, Inc.
CROX.fact: Since Crocs opened its doors in 2002, the company has sold 850+ million shoes.

VAC.name: Marriott Vacations Worldwide Corporation
VAC.fact: The world-renowned Marriott is the owner of The Ritz-Carlton Destination Club, St. Regis, and Grand Residences, just to name a few.

OSUR.name: OraSure Technologies, Inc.
OSUR.fact: Maker of the first over-the-counter home HIV test. OraSure specializes in diagnostic testing kits.

PAL.name: Proficient Auto Logistics, Inc. Common Stock

UNH.name: UnitedHealth Group Incorporated
UNH.fact: In 2017 alone, UnitedHealth Group employees volunteered over 1.5 million hours to help build healthier communities.

EXC.name: Exelon Corporation
EXC.fact: Exelon is one of the largest competitive U.S. power generators, with more than 31,000 megawatts of nuclear, gas, wind, solar, and hydroelectric generating capacity.

DASH.name: DoorDash, Inc.
DASH.fact: DoorDash began in 2012, delivering macaroons in Palo Alto. The company went public in 2021, with revenue of nearly $5 billion. Obviously, they now deliver more than macaroons...

PPL.name: PPL Corporation
PPL.fact: PPL operates approximately 218,000 miles of electric lines. Helicopters are occasionally used to de-ice lines in the winter.

AMSF.name: AMERISAFE, Inc.
AMSF.fact: Amerisafe provides workers' comp insurance in 27 states, helping to provide financial protection to workers - especially those in dangerous occupations - in the event that injury should occur. The company provides extensive safety training to help reduce exposure to accidents.

RBA.name: RB Global, Inc.
RBA.fact: Three brothers, Ken, John, and Ritchie, took over their father's used furniture store. In 1958, the brothers entered their first auction to pay off a small bank loan on short notice. They continued auctioning and their company continues the tradition to this day.

MATX.name: Matson, Inc.
MATX.fact: Alexander & Baldwin began as one of Hawaii's original "Big Five" sugarcane corporations. Some of the company founders were 19th century medical missionaries. Today, A&B is one of Hawaii's largest commercial real estate firms.

HAS.name: Hasbro, Inc.
HAS.fact: Mr. Potato head was the first children's toy that was advertised on television. From 1952 to 1963, parents had to supply real potatoes for the body of Mr. Potato head, until 1964 when Hasbro introduced the hard plastic body.

DD.name: DuPont de Nemours, Inc.
DD.fact: In 1929, Dow hires its first female researcher, Sylvia Stoesser. Five of her patents helped unlock the secrets to treating oil wells.

PDFS.name: PDF Solutions, Inc.
PDFS.fact: PDF Solutions. Inc. helps semiconductor manufacturers test processes, measure, and improve efficiency. Since 1991, the company has made it possible for others to lower cost of design and manufacturing, accelerate time to market, and improve overall product quality and reliability.

COO.name: The Cooper Companies, Inc.
COO.fact: As part of its commitment to supporting local environmental initiatives, CooperVision has adopted five acres of Costa Rica's Osa Peninsula, home to 2.5% of the worlds biodiversity.

COKE.name: Coca-Cola Consolidated, Inc.
COKE.fact: In 1902, J.B. Harrison founded the company that would later become Coca-Cola Consolidated, the largest independent Coca-Cola bottler in the U.S. The great-grandson of J.B. Harrison, J. Frank Harrison, III, held the position of Chairman and CEO.

WCC.name: WESCO International, Inc.
WCC.fact: This Pittsburgh-based electrical company was founded in 1922 and serves approximately 150,000 customers. Its innovative spirit and ingenuity have enabled the company to produce nearly 1.5 million products.

AIT.name: Applied Industrial Technologies, Inc.
AIT.fact: Applied was founded in 1923 by Joeseph Bruening in Cleveland, Ohio. Bearings, power transmission equipment, and fluid control systems are specialties.

HASI.name: HA Sustainable Infrastructure Capital, Inc.
HASI.fact: Hannon Armstrong is the first U.S. public company solely dedicated to investments in climate solutions, with over 320 investments and a portfolio of $3.7 billion as of March 2022.

GRMN.name: Garmin Ltd.
GRMN.fact: Garmin's GPS golf devices give precise distance to the pin, and other features, for thousands of preloaded courses.

GD.name: General Dynamics Corporation
GD.fact: General Dynamics constructs the M1 Abrams Tank, the main battle tank for the United States of America military.

LULU.name: Lululemon Athletica Inc.
LULU.fact: One of the world's top providers of yoga attire, Lululemon opened its first store in the year 2000. Each product undergoes over a dozen tests for quality before approval is granted for production and the company pursues a patent for each new design.

TREX.name: Trex Company, Inc.
TREX.fact: Trex Company is the world's largest manufacturer of wood-alternative decking and railing. The company's composite products are made of 95% recycled materials and it redirects roughly 400 million pounds of plastic and scrap wood from landfills every year.

SYK.name: Stryker Corporation
SYK.fact: In 1942, Stryker started manufacturing the Wedge Turning Frame, which allowed caregivers to turn patients with serious back injuries while keeping them immobilized.

TTGT.name: TechTarget, Inc.
TTGT.fact: Want to know how ot engage technology customers and prospects, and know what they are thinking? TechTarget is all about "purchase intent". The firm helps companies improve engagement, SEO, lead generation, customer intelligence, and client retention through its content, AI, and data service offerings.

BR.name: Broadridge Financial Solutions, Inc.
BR.fact: Broadridge supports communications that reach 75% of North American households.

CARR.name: Carrier Global Corporation
CARR.fact: In 1998, Carrier came up with a unique display case that would help preserve a 500-year old Inca mummy discovered in the Andes in Peru. The embalmed body was brought to Washington and Peru for an exhibit.

PPC.name: Pilgrim's Pride Corporation
PPC.fact: Pilgrim's prides itself in providing more than 133 million daily servings of protein to retailers, restaurants, food services, and consumers with products for sale in over 100 countries.

WMK.name: Weis Markets, Inc.
WMK.fact: Founded in 1912, by Harry and Sigmund Weis, Weis Markets has a special history with ice cream. Headquartered in one of the nation's top dairy-farming states, Weis processes its own milk and uses the excess butterfat to make more than 60 delicious flavors. The company values local farmers and tries to partner with local as much as it can.

AMCR.name: Amcor plc
AMCR.fact: In January 2018, Amcor became the first global packaging company pledging to develop all its packaging to be recyclable or reusable by 2025.

ADNT.name: Adient plc
ADNT.fact: With 208 plants spread across 33 countries, Adient supplies 20 million seat sets on an annual basis, making it a leader in the automotive seating industry.

BOH.name: Bank of Hawaii Corporation
BOH.fact: Founded in 1897, Bank of Hawaii has a long history of weathering changes. Forbes has ranked BOH one of "America's Best Banks" for 11 consecutive years, as of 2021, with a Moody's rating of Aa3 for Long-Term Deposits.

BMI.name: Badger Meter, Inc.
BMI.fact: In business for over 116 years, this company's name pay homage to Wisconsin - its "Badger State" home. Badger Meter's products and service empower management and measurement of water utilities and systems, helping clients to optimize and reduce waste.

HOMB.name: Home Bancshares, Inc.
HOMB.fact: The company was formed in 1998 by John Allison and Robert Adcock Jr. A year later, the company established First State Bank in Conway and has since grown across the United States of America. In 2022, Forbes ranked Home Bancshares as #1 for America's Best Banks.

CEG.name: Constellation Energy Corporation
CEG.fact: Spun-off from Excelon in 2022, Constellation claims to be the largest producer of carbon-free energy in the United States of America.

FRPT.name: Freshpet, Inc.
FRPT.fact: This pet food company was the first to distribute pet food in the fresh and refrigerated category across North America.

SLG.name: SL Green Realty Corp.
SLG.fact: This company is New York City's largest office landlord.

FICO.name: Fair Isaac Corporation
FICO.fact: Founded by Bill Fair and Earl Isaac in 1956, Fair Isaac Corp. is proprietor of the FICO score. Arguably the granddaddy of consumer credit scores, FICO numbers are widely used by banks and other lenders to help make decisions about everything from mortgage qualification to auto loans.

OUST.name: Ouster, Inc.
OUST.fact: Ouster's lidar solutions are used in autonomous vehicles, drones, robotics, security systems, and by the defense industry.

PM.name: Philip Morris International Inc.
PM.fact: Although the Marlboro Man is one of the most widely recognized advertising images in history, a little known fact is that the Marlboro brand was originally marketed in the 1920sas a cigarette for women using the ad slogan "Mild as May."

CRM.name: Salesforce, Inc.
CRM.fact: Over 150,000 companies, both big and small, are growing their business with Salesforce.

ADBE.name: Adobe Inc.
ADBE.fact: Over 90% of the world's creative professionals use Adobe Photoshop. Company co-founder, Charles Geschke, was a graduate of Carnegie Mellon University.

LPLA.name: LPL Financial Holdings Inc.
LPLA.fact: As of 2021, LPL Financial had over $1 trillion in advisory and brokerage assets.

GPRO.name: GoPro, Inc.
GPRO.fact: Founded in 2002, by surfer, skier, and motorsports enthusiast, Nick Woodman, GoPro has a long history of helping people capture amazing adventures on video. It may come as a surpise, but the first protype actually used 35mm film.

AMBA.name: Ambarella, Inc.
AMBA.fact: This Ambarella came four years before Rihanna's version dropped in 2008. The company is a fabless semiconductor designer which began with high-definition H.264 video encoders for the professional broadcast market - making it possible to watch "Umbrella" in crystal clear resolution. Ambarella chips have powered the GoPro Hero, the Dropcam by Nest, and the DJI Phantom series of drones. It is also involved in perception systems and autonomous vehicle components.

KOP.name: Koppers Holdings Inc.
KOP.fact: Founded in 1912. by a German immigrant named Heinrich Koppers, this company is one of the largest providers of railroad crossties. Koppers  three divisions are: Railroad and Utility Products & Services, Performance Chemicals, and Carbon Materials and Chemicals.

MPB.name: Mid Penn Bancorp, Inc.
MPB.fact: Founded in 1868, as the "Millersburg Trust Company", Mid Penn  has a proud history, including recognition as a "Best Bank to Work For" by American Banker magazine. A full-service financial institution, company operates over three dozen retail locations across Pennsylvania.

RIOT.name: Riot Platforms, Inc.
RIOT.fact: Riot Blockchain is one of the largest publicly-traded Bitcoin mining companies in North America.

CDLX.name: Cardlytics, Inc.
CDLX.fact: Cardlytics is an advertising platform for banks' digital channels. It makes it possible for banks to see where and when customers buy, both online and in-store. This helps banks target customers and direct ads. As of 2022, the company reported tracking 170 million monthly active users.

CYRX.name: Cryoport, Inc.
CYRX.fact: Cryoport claims to be the life sciences industry's most trusted provider of temperature-controlled supply chain solutions.

DGX.name: Quest Diagnostics Incorporated
DGX.fact: Quest Diagnostics Drug Testing Index (DTI) reports examine trends in workplace drug testing and have been considered a benchmark for U.S. workforce drug positivity trends since 1988.

PCG.name: PG&E Corporation
PCG.fact: PG&E has over 106,681 circuit miles of electric distribution lines, 42,141 miles of natural gas distribution pipelines and 6,438 miles of transmission pipelines.

PWR.name: Quanta Services, Inc.
PWR.fact: Quanta is the largest specialty contractor in North America.

VNO.name: Vornado Realty Trust
VNO.fact: Vornado owns 20.2 million square feet of Manhattan office space, across 36 properties. It also bought Chicago's famous Merchandise Mart, one of the largest buildings ever constructed (by floor area), from the Kennedy family, and co-owns San Francisco's 555 California Street with Donald Trump.

ESTC.name: Elastic N.V.
ESTC.fact: This American-Dutch-based company offers its state-of-the-art technology to several big-name tech companies including Uber, eBay, Netflix, Tinder, Lyft, and more.

PINS.name: Pinterest, Inc.
PINS.fact: Pinterest's social media and image sharing platform has over 450 million monthly active users, with half living outside of the U.S.

CNC.name: Centene Corp.
CNC.fact: Centene offers affordable and high-quality products to nearly 1 in 15 individuals across the nation.

FAST.name: Fastenal Company
FAST.fact: Fastenal Employees have engaged in over 127,000 safety, coaching, training, and inspection events. The company is based in the same Winona, Minnesota that actress Winona Ryder is named after.

TOL.name: Toll Brothers, Inc.
TOL.fact: Operating in 24 states, Toll Brothers is the United States of America top builder of luxury homes. The average selling price of a Toll home in 2020 was $816,500.

MSA.name: MSA Safety Incorporated
MSA.fact: A horrific workplace tragedy that led to the creation of MSA, the worldwide leader in worker protection and safety product innovation. On the morning of March 26, 1912, the Jed Mine in West Virginia exploded. In a flash, methane gas ignited and more than 80 miners lost their lives. From this tragedy, mine engineer John T. Ryan Sr. had an epiphany: "If I could spend my life doing what I can to lessen the likelihood of the occurrence of such terrible disasters, I shall feel in the end that my life had been well spent." Ryan recruited colleague George H. Deike to help realize his vision for a new company. Recognizing the critical importance of dependable, safe mining equipment, they went straight to one of the country's great thinkers: Thomas Edison. The brilliant inventor helped Ryan and Deike create the electric cap lamp which, over the next 25 years, reduced mine explosions by an astounding 75 percent. Of all his inventions, this was the one that did the most for humanity, Edison would later say in life.

DAL.name: Delta Air Lines, Inc.

JBL.fact: The leading technology company was founded when young entrepreneurial founders began assembling circuit boards around the kitchen table in Michigan. The company now operates in over 50 million square feet of manufacturing space with over 260 thousand employees worldwide.

MIDD.name: The Middleby Corporation
MIDD.fact: The company was founded in 1888 as a bakery supplier. As of 2018, the company had nearly 10,000 employees.

CPS.name: Cooper-Standard Holdings Inc.
CPS.fact: Cooper Standard makes rubber and plastic sealing, fuel and brake lines, fluid transfer hoses, and anti-vibration systems for the auto industry. Its proprietary Fortrex product is an advanced polymer that can deliver weight savings up to 30% versus conventional products.

INTC.name: Intel Corp.
INTC.fact: Intel has a museum which has different artifacts and interesting facts about Intel. This museum was started in the early 1980s and was opened to public in 1992. You will get to know various interesting facts about the 40+ years old semiconductor company.

BWXT.name: BWX Technologies, Inc.
BWXT.fact: BWX has spent 60+ years in nuclear innovation, with over 400 reactors delivered for Naval Nuclear Power and more than 314 steam generators delivered to nuclear power plants.

REGN.name: Regeneron Pharmaceuticals, Inc.
REGN.fact: Regeneron received considerable press as one of the companies at the forefront of development for experimental COVID-19 treatments.

CVNA.name: Carvana Co.
CVNA.fact: Did you ever think that vending machines for cars would be a thing? Well, Carvana did... and in February of 2022, they sold their 1 millionth car.

TRGP.name: Targa Resources Corp.
TRGP.fact: Targa Resources is a Fortune 500 company with just under 3,000 employees.

CAG.name: Conagra Brands, Inc.
CAG.fact: Conagra owns the Slim Jim brand.

ACHC.name: Acadia Healthcare Company, Inc.
ACHC.fact: With approximately 70,000 patients served daily, Acadia is the largest stand-alone behavioral health company in the U.S.

NVT.name: nVent Electric plc
NVT.fact: nVent traces its roots back to 1903, back when very few homes had the luxury of electricity. Several decades later, an invention that stopped machinery when workers' hands got too close enabled the company to flourish for many years to come.

GWW.name: W.W. Grainger, Inc.
GWW.fact: On average, their customers have a 17-year history of buying from Grainger - that's serious brand-loyalty!

CHDN.name: Churchill Downs Incorporated
CHDN.fact: In 1875, Meriwether Lewis Clark developed a racetrack to showcase Kentucky's legendary horse breeding industry, thus launching the world-renowned Kentucky Derby. Churchill Downs Incorporated has since acquired more racetracks, casinos, and online wagering platforms.

LDOS.name: Leidos Holdings, Inc.
LDOS.fact: Leidos predecessor company, SAIC, played a vital role in cleaning up the 3 mile island nuclear disaster.

JNJ.name: Johnson & Johnson
JNJ.fact: Johnson & Johnson's inventions were presented alongside Nikola Tesla and Thomas Edison's inventions at the 1893 World Fair.

TMO.name: Thermo Fisher Scientific Inc.
TMO.fact: Thermo-Fischer has a section of their website dedicated to their research on cloning DNA!

HWC.name: Hancock Whitney Corporation
HWC.fact: Hancock County Bank was founded in 1899 with only $10,000 in capital, but the bank experienced tremendous growth by serving the needs of the booming trade of Mississippi.

HRL.name: Hormel Foods Corporation
HRL.fact: In 1926, the company introduced Hormel Flavor-Sealed Ham, America's first canned ham.

SWKS.name: Skyworks Solutions, Inc.
SWKS.fact: Nearly half of Skyworks' revenue is generated from producing wireless chips for Apple.

MO.name: Altria Group, Inc.
MO.fact: In 1978, Altria, then Philip Morris, purchased the Seven-Up Company.

MKL.name: Markel Corporation
MKL.fact: The company was founded by Samuel Markel in 1930 and his three sons would later join the growing business as it continued to flourish.

EEFT.name: Euronet Worldwide, Inc.
EEFT.fact: In 2021, Euronet processed 7.6 billion transactions in 175 countries.

HELE.name: Helen of Troy Limited
HELE.fact: As you might have guessed, the company is named after the mythical figure, Helen of Troy. No word if Brad Pitt has visited their HQ.

EXP.name: Eagle Materials Inc.
EXP.fact: Eagle Materials is an American company and makes that clear to everyone - all of its manufactured products are 100% made in the USA.

AZZ.name: AZZ Inc.
AZZ.fact: AZZ Inc. claims to be North America's largest hot-dip galvanizer. The company uses its state-of-the-art dip tanks to coat and protect components, primarily those made of metal, for durable use in the most environmentally demanding applications. Major clients include the energy and infrastructure industries.

NEE.name: NextEra Energy, Inc.
NEE.fact: Nextera is one of America's largest capital investors in infrastructure. Around $50-55 billion in infrastructure investments are planned to be made through 2022.

GTES.name: Gates Industrial Corporation plc
GTES.fact: In 1911, Charles Gates acquired a tire and rubber company, and a few years later, Gates invented the V-belt. With over 100 years of experience, Gate's company has grown to over 100 locations in 30 countries pushing to be the best fluid power and power transmission company in the world.

ADM.name: Archer-Daniels-Midland Company
ADM.fact: In 1986, ADM formed the Golden Peanut Company.

RDN.name: Radian Group Inc.
RDN.fact: Understanding the vast opportunities of digital technology, Radian pioneered the first-ever ML rate quote app, "Radian Rates."

FCN.name: FTI Consulting, Inc.
FCN.fact: FTI is an advisor to 98 of the world's top 100 law firms, 9 of the world's top 10 bank holding companies, and 59 of the Fortune Global 100 corporations.

CLX.name: The Clorox Company
CLX.fact: The company's first product, Clorox liquid bleach, was packaged in five-gallon returnable containers and delivered by horse-drawn wagon to local breweries, dairies, and laundries for cleaning and disinfecting their facilities.

MCY.name: Mercury General Corporation
MCY.fact: Founded in 1961, Mercury General is an insurance company with approximately $6 billion in assets. It has been named to "America's Most Trustowrthy Companies" by Forbes on multiple occasions.

RGA.name: Reinsurance Group of America, Incorporated
RGA.fact: RGA had approximately $3.5 trillion of life reinsurance in force and $92.2 billion in assets as of 2021.

URI.name: United Rentals, Inc.
URI.fact: United Rentals is the largest equipment rental company in North America, with about 13% of the market share. They own the largest rental fleet of equipment with about 660,000 rental units.

WU.name: The Western Union Company
WU.fact: In 1974, the company made history. It brought the United States of America its very first commercial satellite.

PRU.name: Prudential Financial, Inc.
PRU.fact: Prudential Financial is the largest insurance company in the United States of America, with total assets of about $1.5 trillion.

CIEN.name: Ciena Corporation
CIEN.fact: This telecommunications company's customers include some of the world's largest mobile telephones services such as AT&T, T-Mobile, and Verizon.

SHW.name: The Sherwin-Williams Company
SHW.fact: In 1940 Canadian Norman Breakey invented the first paint roller. He didn't profit from it because he never patented it. During World War II, an inventor working for Sherwin-Williams also created a roller brush because the hogs hair used for paintbrushes was unavailable due to the war.

CW.name: Curtiss-Wright Corporation
CW.fact: Curtis-Wright claims to have the most renowned legacy in the aerospace industry after having been formed by the titans of aviation Glenn Curtis, the father of naval aviation, and the Wright brothers, who were credited with the first flight of mankind. When the company consolidated in 1929, it immediately became the country's largest aviation company, which positioned it nicely to build over 142,000 aircraft for the U.S. military during WWII.

FOXF.name: Fox Factory Holding Corp.
FOXF.fact: Fox Factory Holding recently acquired three manufacturing companies that specifically cater to sport trucks.

BSY.name: Bentley Systems, Incorporated
BSY.fact: Bentley Systems is also a publisher (Bentley Institute Press) of textbooks and professional references that include a wide variety of educational and practical sources for AEC, operations, geospatial, and educational communities.

UBER.name: Uber Technologies, Inc.
UBER.fact: Founded in 2009, Uber makes it easy for people to find a ride - especially in places where taxi service is difficult or limited. The company  has grown to serve more than 900 cities worldwide, with over 5 billion Uber trips each year.

ZBRA.name: Zebra Technologies Corporation
ZBRA.fact: Zebra Technologies currently has over 4,900 patents that are awaiting approval.

FITB.name: Fifth Third Bancorp
FITB.fact: Fifth Third Field is the name of 5 different stadiums. 3 of them are for minor league baseball teams.

DCI.name: Donaldson Company, Inc.
DCI.fact: Donaldson Company started as an engineering business. Its most important client during the foundational years was the Deere & Company.

EHC.name: Encompass Health Corporation
EHC.fact: Encompass Health is one of the largest providers of post-acute healthcare services and is a component of the S&P 400.

OTIS.name: Otis Worldwide Corporation
OTIS.fact: The steel frame and the Otis elevator are widely considered to be the two biggest stepping stones into the world of skyscrapers. The needs of the modern building are changing, however, as energy prices climb higher and higher. New elevators from Otis, like the Gen2 Switch, are solar-capable.

SON.name: Sonoco Products Company
SON.fact: The company was originally named the Southern Novelty Company but, in 1923, changed its name to 'Sonoco," using the first two letters of each word.

ARI.name: Apollo Commercial Real Estate Finance, Inc.

KBR.name: KBR, Inc.
KBR.fact: Kellogg's innovation led to the creation of new technologies and industry milestones, including the revolutionized fertilizer production through the creation of a new ammonia process, making rapid growth in global food production possible. Kellogg Brown merged with Brown & Root to create KBR.

TFC.name: Truist Financial Corporation
TFC.fact: Truist Financial is the 6th largest U.S. commercial bank, having over $488 billion in assets.

NG.name: NovaGold Resources Inc.
NG.fact: NovaGold is a pure gold play focused on Alaska's Donlin Gold prospect - one of the world's largest gold mines, with 39 million ounces of estimated mineral resource.

CHD.name: Church & Dwight Co., Inc.
CHD.fact: The ARM & HAMMER logo symbolized the myth of Vulcan, the Roman god of fire, who would strike his mighty hammer on his anvil. Over time, this strong and powerful icon became recognized as a symbol of quality all across the world.

PLD.name: Prologis, Inc.
PLD.fact: Prologis built a 270,000 SF industrial warehouse in Mexico for Cooper Tire & Rubber Company.

ADI.name: Analog Devices, Inc.
ADI.fact: ADI operates Ireland's largest semiconductor R&D center in Limerick.

KR.name: The Kroger Co.
KR.fact: Kroger produces about 40% of the corporate brand units sold in its stores.

IDA.name: IDACORP, Inc.
IDA.fact: With more than 100 years of experience, this Idaho power company has set a goal to achieve 100% clean energy by 2045.

UFPI.name: UFP Industries, Inc.
UFPI.fact: UFP shipped its first load of treated lumber to The Home Depot in 1979, which was a brand new company at the time.

UTHR.name: United Therapeutics Corporation
UTHR.fact: The founder of this biotechnology company established it after her daughter was diagnosed with a fatal orphan disease known as PAH.

ACM.name: Aecom
ACM.fact: AECOM was ranked number 1 by Fortune magazine as the World's Most Admired Company in its industry (Infrastructure Consulting) in 2021.

TTWO.name: Take-Two Interactive Software, Inc.
TTWO.fact: This company owns the Rockstar Games label. They are responsible for designing hit videogames in the Grand Theft Auto and Red Dead Redemption series, among others.

SFIX.name: Stitch Fix, Inc.
SFIX.fact: Stitch Fix was originally called Rack Habit and was run out of the apartment of one of the founders, Katrina Lake.

NEOG.name: Neogen Corporation
NEOG.fact: Neogen was founded in 1982 as an investment project by Michigan State University. Three years later, the biotech company developed the first rapid test for mycotoxins.

AGO.name: Assured Guaranty Ltd.
AGO.fact: The financial strength of Assured Guaranty is reflected in the $11 billion in total claims paying resources across the Assured Guaranty Group.

MRK.name: Merck & Co., Inc.
MRK.fact: After the U.S entered World War I, the Merck Group's US subsidiary Merck & Co. was confiscated under the Trading with the Enemy Act of 1917. Company head, George W. Merck, purchased back the stock in 1919, but U.S. Merck remained a separate company from its former German parent.

F.name: Ford Motor Company
F.fact: Henry Ford and Thomas Edison were lifelong friends. As requested by Ford, Thomas Edison's son captured Edison's last exhale in a test tube and sealed it with a cork. Ford kept the tube as a memorial to Edison's "life and breath".

APD.name: Air Products and Chemicals, Inc.
APD.fact: In the mid-1950's Air Products gained an opportunity from the launching of the first Sputnik, which American scientists surmised was powered by liquid hydrogen. The U.S. also wanted liquid hydrogen, and Air Products was asked to supply it. As a security precaution, the new Air Products Company plants were provided with code names like "Baby-Bear" and "Project Rover". One large plant was disguised as the "Apix Fertilizer Company".

NWL.name: Newell Brands Inc.
NWL.fact: During World War II, Western Newell converted factories to assist with the war effort, earning the Army/Navy "E" award for excellence in wartime production.

FCNCA.name: First Citizens BancShares, Inc.
FCNCA.fact: The bank was founded in 1898 in a rural town in North Carolina with only $10,000 worth of capital and served primarily agriculture customers.

ALHC.name: Alignment Healthcare, Inc.
ALHC.fact: Alignment Healthcare was created after CEO John Kao was caring for his ailing mother and disabled brother and did not feel they were receiving the necessary care from a disconnected health care system. He wanted to change that, so he founded Alignment in 2013.

EW.name: Edwards Lifesciences Corporation
EW.fact: Edwards Lifesciences roots date to 1958 when Miles Lowell Edwards set out to build the first artificial heart.

RJF.name: Raymond James Financial, Inc.
RJF.fact: Edward Raymond sold Raymond and Associates to Bob James, with the agreement that Bob will name the new firm Raymond James & Associates. Soon after, Ed suffers a near-fatal car accident and never joins the firm. Bob, however, insists on keeping Ed's name on the door, ahead of his own. Yes - both gentlemen had first names for last names.

RRC.name: Range Resources Corporation
RRC.fact: As of the end of 2021, Range Resources had 17.775 trillion cubic feet of natural gas equivalent of estimated proved reserves. Most of the land they own is in the Marcellus Shale.

AMZN.name: Amazon.com, Inc.
AMZN.fact: The company was originally called Cadabra, like the magic term "abracadabra." But Jeff Bezos' lawyer told him that the magic reference was too obscure, and when you say it out loud, "cadabra" could be mistaken for "cadaver." Eventually, they came up with the name Amazon, a reference to the river in South America. The idea was that their selection of books would be vast and wide, just like the world's largest river.

IPAR.name: Inter Parfums, Inc.
IPAR.fact: Founded in 1982, Inter Parfums USA develops, manufactures, and distributes prestige perfumes and cosmetics as the exclusive worldwide licensee for Abercrombie & Fitch, Anna Sui, Dunhill, Graff, GUESS, Hollister, MCM, Oscar de la Renta.

PPG.name: PPG Industries, Inc.
PPG.fact: PPG has a long history of innovation. Started in 1883, the company was instrumental in breaking European monopoly on the production of plate glass. Within 40 years, PPG had become the largest glass producer in the nation. In the 1950's, the company developed the first latex-based interior paints. Today, the company researches, develops, and manufactures some of the most advanced coatings on the planet.

THRY.name: Thryv Holdings, Inc.
THRY.fact: Although Thryv's history goes back over 125 years, it has been a very adaptive company. In its present evolution, Thryv software solutions and services have helped over 300,000 small businesses secure clients, manage relationships, and/or obtain credit.

CHTR.name: Charter Communications, Inc.
CHTR.fact: There are 33 Spectrum networks delivering local news and sports.

GSAT.name: Globalstar, Inc.
GSAT.fact: Globalstar operates 48 low earth orbit (LEO) satellites. The company is able to provide reliable communication even to areas without cellular coverage or any other communications infrastructure. Globalstar has a proud history of its devices being used in many search and rescue, and disaster recovery operations.

SO.name: The Southern Company
SO.fact: This company has an energy trading floor that is open 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.

R.name: Ryder System, Inc.
R.fact: With a $35 down payment on a Ford truck, Jim Ryder started a business hauling concrete. He wore two wristwatches, one on each arm, to remind his customers of his commitment to timely deliveries. He even hauled supplies for the U.S. government during WWII. From the humble origins of a one man/one truck crew, the Ryder business has since grown to more than 272,000 vehicles managed and 55 million square feet of warehouse space.

AGNC.name: AGNC Investment Corp.
AGNC.fact: REIT specializing in Agency RMBS, collateralized borrowing structures, and repurchase agreements.

CTOS.name: Custom Truck One Source, Inc.
CTOS.fact: Custom Truck One Source is a leading provider of specialized trucks and heavy equipment, including (but not limited to) Boom Trucks, Cranes, Dump Trucks, Forestry Trucks, Waste & Refuse Trucks, Service / Utility Trucks, and Vac Trucks.

IRDM.name: Iridium Communications Inc.
IRDM.fact: The first satellite was launched by the Russians, and they called the machinery the "Sputnik." Forty-one years later, Vice President of the United States of America Al Gore made a call to the great-grandson of Alexander Graham Bell using an Iridium satellite. The name "Iridium" comes from the chemical element iridium which has an atomic number of 77, which represented the number of satellites the company initially planned to deploy.

TNL.name: Travel + Leisure Co.
TNL.fact: Travel + Leisure owns a diverse portfolio of hospitality centers including Wyndham Destinations, Panorama, and of course the Travel + Leisure Group.

CF.name: CF Industries Holdings, Inc.
CF.fact: CF manufactures dozens of nitrogen products for agricultural and industrial uses.

LRCX.name: Lam Research Corporation
LRCX.fact: In 1988, this company invented single-wafer spin clean technology. Clean silicon wafers = higher chip manufacturing yields.

MTDR.name: Matador Resources Company
MTDR.fact: Joseph Foran and Scott King founded Matador Resources Company with an initial $6 million investment to show how confident they were in their future endeavor. This sparked an additional $46.8 million from various investors, which enabled the company to expand to what it is now.

CTVA.name: Corteva, Inc.
CTVA.fact: Former U.S. vice president Henry Wallace founded Hi-Bred Corn Company, one of Corteva's predecessor company's.

DXCM.name: DexCom, Inc.
DXCM.fact: Dexcom was founded based on the groundbreaking research of Dr. Stuart J. Updike and George P. Hicks in 1967  implantable, long-performing glucose sensors that the body would not reject.

APPF.name: AppFolio Inc.
APPF.fact: With over 17,000 customers and 6+ million units managed, it does not come as a surprise that in 2021, AppFolio ranked #11 on Fortune’s list of the 100 Fastest Growing Companies.

CMC.name: Commercial Metals Company
CMC.fact: Commercial Metals Company's rebar can be found in many structures - including the AT&T Stadium in Dallas, the Pentagon, essential highways and bridges, and other modern landmarks all over the world.

AAON.name: AAON, Inc.
AAON.fact: AAON has offices and manufacturing facilities in Tulsa, Oklahoma, which has more than 1.51 million square feet.

WTS.name: Watts Water Technologies, Inc.
WTS.fact: A 17-year-old emigrated from England to Massachusetts to seek his fortune. In 1874, he started his own company known as Watts Regulator Company. In addition to running his business, Joseph Watts achieved widespread fame as the patentee and maker of steam and water pressure regulators. His ingenuity started a company that has endured for well over 100 years.

MOV.name: Movado Group, Inc.
MOV.fact: Known as a maker of luxury timepieces, Movado's most famous brand ambassador is arguably former Public Enemy MC, Flavor Flav - also known for his hit show "Flavor of Love".

CRMT.name: America's Car-Mart, Inc.
CRMT.fact: One of America's largest used car dealer  networks, the company operated 154 locations acrpss the South-Central U.S.

RS.name: Reliance Steel & Aluminum Co.
RS.fact: The steel company was founded in 1939 by Thomas Neilan and largely produced rebar. Now the company distributes approximately 100,000 different metal products.

NRG.name: NRG Energy, Inc.
NRG.fact: Committed to a 50% reduction in carbon emissions by 2030 and working toward a 90% reduction by 2050.

OZK.name: Bank OZK
OZK.fact: Bank OZK's roots date back to its establishment as a community bank for a little town in Arkansas in 1903.

ETSY.name: Etsy, Inc.
ETSY.fact: Etsy seller live all over the world in 234 countries, but 62% of them live in the United States of America.

MTN.name: Vail Resorts, Inc.
MTN.fact: The co-founders of the company, Pete Seibert and Earl Eaton, shared dream of finding the next great ski mountain. Eaton was a lifelong resident of the area and led Siebert, who served in the United States of America Army during WWII, to the beautiful mountain in Colorado. Vail Resorts now has forty mountain resorts in three countries.

CBOE.name: Cboe Global Markets, Inc.
CBOE.fact: In 1973, Cboe was founded and became the first marketplace for trading listed options.

IQV.name: IQVIA Holdings Inc.
IQV.fact: Iqvia's algorithm to detect diseases improved accuracy from 1/70,000 to 1/7.

POOL.name: Pool Corporation
POOL.fact: Modern-day swimming pools became popular in Britain in the mid-1800s. By 1837 there were six indoor pools in London, complete with diving boards.

HLF.name: Herbalife Nutrition Ltd.
HLF.fact: Herbalife Nutrition is the #1 brand in active and lifestyle nutrition, and the numbers do not lie. In 2021, 5.4 million Herbalife Nutrition protein shakes were consumed daily.

THC.name: Tenet Healthcare Corporation
THC.fact: This healthcare company operates more than 60 hospitals and 430 healthcare facilities.

UPS.name: United Parcel Service, Inc.
UPS.fact: In 1927, UPS was one of the first companies in the nation to offer their employees shares of the company. Today UPS is primarily owned by its employees; only ten percent of UPS stock is available to the public.

WDC.name: Western Digital Corporation
WDC.fact: In 2001, Western Digital became the first manufacturer to offer mainstream ATA hard disk drives with 8MBofdisk buffer. At that time, most desktop hard disk drives had 2MB of buffer.

KEY.name: KeyCorp
KEY.fact: Keycorp has earned the National Organization on Disabilities' Leading Disability Employer Seal three years in a row.

BH.name: Biglari Holdings Inc.
BH.fact: ConocoPhillips produced 1,348 barrels of oil per day in 2019.

CBRE.name: CBRE Group, Inc.
CBRE.fact: CBRE's Global Cost Trends Guide captures data from 134 cities in 75 countries to shed light on both current and prospective cost trends across North America, EMEA, Asia Pacific, and Latin America.

ALGT.name: Allegiant Travel Company
ALGT.fact: Allegiant Travel is an ultra low-cost U.S. airline and one of the 15 largest in North America.

WTRG.name: Essential Utilities, Inc.
WTRG.fact: The company dates its roots back to the founding of the Springfield Water Company in 1886.

IPGP.name: IPG Photonics Corporation
IPGP.fact: This company is the leading developer and manufacturer of high-performance fiber lasers. Recommended watch - Val Kilmer in the classic comedy "Real Genius"

ED.name: Consolidated Edison, Inc.
ED.fact: Consolidated Edison has invested over $4 billion in renewable projects, across 17 states. Following recent acquisitions, it is the second largest solar producer in North America.

CSGP.name: CoStar Group, Inc.
CSGP.fact: Founded in 1987, CoStar is a leading data and analytics provider to the commercial real estate industry. Major subsidiaries include Apartment Finder, Apartments.com, LoopNet, Homes.com, LandsofAmerica, and HomesSnap.

KFY.name: Korn Ferry
KFY.fact: The PGA announced Korn Ferry as the umbrella sponsor of the newly named Korn Ferry Tour in 2019 - 3 out of 4 PGA Tour members are Korn Ferry Tour alumni.

RUN.name: Sunrun Inc.
RUN.fact: Sunrun is a rival of Elon Musk-backed SolarCity in the market to provide residential solar panels and energy storage.

QLYS.name: Qualys, Inc.
QLYS.fact: More than 10,000 customers worldwide trust Qualys, with 46% of Forbes Global 500 being among the satisfied customers.

HE.name: Hawaiian Electric Industries, Inc.
HE.fact: Hawaiian Electric Industries supplies power to 95% of Hawaii's population, though it does not serve the island of Kauai. The company was founded in 1891 - ten years after Hawaii's King Kalakaua met Thomas Edison in New York. The King's Iolani Palace was one of the world's first royal residences to be powered by electricity.

FE.name: FirstEnergy Corp.
FE.fact: FirstEnergy uses drones to monitor birds nests on their transmission towers.

KEYS.name: Keysight Technologies, Inc.
KEYS.fact: Keysight is part of the Hewlett-Packard family tree and was spun off from Agilent (itself, having been spun off of HP).

DE.name: Deere & Company
DE.fact: In 1837, inspired by the back-breaking difficulty farmers experienced near his home in Grand Detour, Illinois, John Deere acquired a broken steel saw blade, and from it, created a new type of moldboard plow.

SPB.name: Spectrum Brands Holdings, Inc.
SPB.fact: Spectrum Brands prides itself in providing home essentials to millions of consumers all over the world with brands like Baldwin, National Hardware, Cutter, and more.

NCLH.name: Norwegian Cruise Line Holdings Ltd.
NCLH.fact: Glow-in-the-dark bowling is available on board Norwegian Cruise Line ships.

SONO.name: Sonos, Inc.
SONO.fact: Sonos is considered the pioneer of wireless audio, with the Arc being one of its prized products. Since it was founded in 2002, the tech company has spread across 50+ streaming services with well over 500 patents.

DCOM.name: Dime Community Bancshares, Inc.
DCOM.fact: Dime Community Bank was started in 1864 to serve a need in the immigrant community for banking services. The company remained privately held for 132 years, until going public in 1996.

EMR.name: Emerson Electric Co.
EMR.fact: In 1890, Emerson was founded as a manufacturer of electric motors and fans.

G.name: Genpact Limited
G.fact: As of 2022, the company had over 100,000 employees in more than 30 countries.

TNK.name: Teekay Tankers Ltd.
TNK.fact: Teekay claims to be the world's largest operator of mid-sized tankers. Its "SuezMax" tankers are classified as such because they are the largest size ship that will still fit through the Suez Canal.

APA.name: APA Corporation
APA.fact: Apache Oil Corporation was founded on December 6, 1954, in Minneapolis by Truman Anderson, Raymond Plank, and Charles Arnao. The company started with six employees and $250,000 in funding. The company's name started with the founders' initials A, P, and A. Che was added to the end at the suggestion of Helen Johnson, an early employee who was awarded a $25 U.S. savings bond for the idea.

SPT.name: Sprout Social, Inc.
SPT.fact: If you needed to manage multiple social media accounts for a business - and get detailed analytics - Sprout Social might be able to help. The company offers popular software solutions for content creators seeking help managing their digital brand.

OC.name: Owens Corning
OC.fact: The Pink Panther regularly appears as the company's mascot, showing up in most of the advertisement for the world's largest manufacturer of fiberglass composites.

ENPH.name: Enphase Energy, Inc.
ENPH.fact: In 1977, a single watt of solar energy cost over $76 per panel. Because of technological advancements from many companies, including Enphase, the price per watt for solar panels is now between $2 and $3.

GLW.name: Corning Inc
GLW.fact: This company manufactures Gorilla Glass, which is used by smartphone makers around the world.

QCOM.name: QUALCOMM Incorporated
QCOM.fact: Qualcomm Wireless Reach brings advanced wireless technologies to underserved communities globally, improving lives with programs that strengthen economic and social development. Since 2006, Wireless Reach has impacted over 13 million beneficiaries.

PCOR.name: Procore Technologies, Inc.
PCOR.fact: The Founder of Procore, Craig "Tooey" Courtemanche, created software that would enable him to manage the construction of his home in Santa Barbara. In 2021, the app he built had over 10,000 customers with over 1.5 million users spanning across 125 countries.

GNTX.name: Gentex Corporation
GNTX.fact: The company leverages over 125 years of history and producers a diversified portfolio of products that range from hearing protection to defense and security products. The largest portion of its sales comes from auto-dimming mirrors that go to almost every major automaker in the world.

BRK-B.name: Berkshire Hathaway Inc.
BRK-B.fact: Warren Buffett acquired Berkshire Hathaway in 1965, when the company was a struggling textile manufacturer. Today, it is one of the world's largest holding company conglomerates, with interests in many industries.

MCD.name: McDonald's Corporation
MCD.fact: In 1961, McDonald's founder Ray Kroc launched a training program, later called Hamburger University, at a new McDonalds restaurant in Elk Grove Village, Illinois. There, franchisees were trained on proper methods for running a successful McDonalds restaurant, using a research and development laboratory in nearby Addison, Illinois to develop new cooking, freezing, storing, and serving methods. Today, more than 275,000 franchisees, managers, and employees have graduated from the program.

ESS.name: Essex Property Trust, Inc.
ESS.fact: In 2010, Essex increased their regular dividend. They were the only multifamily REIT to do so during the Great Recession.

GALT.name: Galectin Therapeutics Inc.
GALT.fact: Chronic liver disease and cancer are the focus of Galectin, which is a pioneer in research and development of new drugs and therapies.

DNLI.name: Denali Therapeutics Inc.
DNLI.fact: Denali has embarked on a journey to develop drugs that address diseases such as Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, and ALS.

CCL.name: Carnival Corporation & plc
CCL.fact: Carnival Cruise Line was launched in 1972 with just one second-hand ship and just enough fuel to make a one-way trip from Miami to San Juan.

ATI.name: ATI Inc.
ATI.fact: A company with a rich history of engineering, manufacturing, and invention, ATI is engaged in research, development, and manufacturing of advanced metals and superalloys. ATI products are used in some of the world's most demanding material applications, including aerospace, defense, mining, and advanced medicine, among others.

CENX.name: Century Aluminum Company
CENX.fact: With operations in the U.S., Iceland, and Netherlands, Century Aluminum manufactures high quality, high purity aluminum and carbon anodes.

KHC.name: The Kraft Heinz Company
KHC.fact: Heinz sells more single-serve ketchup packets annually than there are people on earth.

LAW.name: CS Disco, Inc.
LAW.fact: Disco brings AI technology to over 900 law firms worldwide. Its goal is to reinvent legal technology to automate and simplify complex and error-prone tasks that distract from practicing law.

ICUI.name: ICU Medical, Inc.
ICUI.fact: George "Doc" Lopez, founder of ICU Medical, is known for the development of the product called ClickLock, which secures I.V. lines to patients so that they are not accidentally stuck or disconnected.

LOW.name: Lowe's Companies, Inc.
LOW.fact: Lowe's and its namesake foundation have pledged to invest $350 million in different communities by 2025.

PAR.name: PAR Technology Corporation
PAR.fact: PTC's revolutionary Creo product design software allows users to create comprehensive virtual prototypes of products.

BX.name: Blackstone Inc.
BX.fact: Specializing in investment management, Blackstone is a major player in private equity, alternatives, and real estate. Representative clients include pension funds, large institutions, and ultra-high net worth individuals.

IRTC.name: iRhythm Technologies, Inc.
IRTC.fact: iRhythm is a medical technonology company dedicated to helping individuals with heart conditions and the physicians who care for them. Monitors like the Zio XT and Zio AT attach to the chest, without wires, and deliver high-quality accurate data to help ensure that heart behavior is regular or to warn in event of a medical problem.

CRC.name: California Resources Corp
CRC.fact: CRC is committed to energy transition in the sector and has some of the lowest carbon intensity production in the U.S.

CTAS.name: Cintas Corporation
CTAS.fact: 5 million+ people who work for other companies get ready for their day by putting on a Cintas-made uniform.

WSBC.name: WesBanco, Inc.
WSBC.fact: WesBanco's founding dates back to 1870 when the original charter was issued as "The German Bank," in Wheeling, West Virginia. The company experienced many mergers and acquisitions - and endured natural disasters, recessions, and depressions - but has pushed throughall adversities to become one of the largest banks in West Virginia. It is also the namesake of WesBanco Arena, home of the Wheeling Nailers hockey team.

FUBO.name: fuboTV Inc.
FUBO.fact: fuboTV is considered the world's only sports-focused live TV streaming service with some of the top leagues and teams. With over 100 channels varying from sports to entertainment, fuboTV enables access to the NFL, NBA, MLB, MLS, and more.

USFD.name: US Foods Holding Corp.
USFD.fact: The food provider traces its roots back to a company founded in 1853, which was designed to provision wagon trains heading west during the gold rush.

BEAM.name: Beam Therapeutics Inc.
BEAM.fact: Beam Therapeutics traces its origins to the Broad Institute, a highly credited research center of MIT and Harvard University. Before the company went public, it raised over $1 billion in VC funds.

PEP.name: PepsiCo, Inc.
PEP.fact: Pepsi-Cola was the first American product to be manufactured, marketed, and sold in the Soviet Union.

ETN.name: Eaton Corporation plc
ETN.fact: Eaton's spirit and innovation started in 1911 when a young entrepreneur named Joseph Eaton decided to invest in the first gear-driven truck axle.

LIVN.name: LivaNova PLC
LIVN.fact: LivaNova, a producer of medical devices, was formed in 2015 after Cyberonics and Sorin merged in a 2.7 billion dollar deal.

TXG.name: 10x Genomics, Inc.
TXG.fact: Serge Saxonov founded the company in 2012. Before becoming CEO and Co-founder of 10x Genomics, Serge was the first employee at 23andME, where he served as Founding Architect and Director of R&D.

IBM.name: International Business Machines Corporation
IBM.fact: Five IBM employees have won the Nobel Prize. The company has also been granted over 140,000 patents, since 1920 - the most in the S&P 500.

WAB.name: Westinghouse Air Brake Technologies Corporation
WAB.fact: A global leader in freight trains, Wabtec moves over 20% of the world's freight with about 23,000 locomotives across six continents. Company founder and serial entrepreneur, George Westinghouse, was arguably the Elon Musk of the 19th century. After enlisting in the New York National Guard at the age of 15, he became self-taught in engineering and had invented the rotary steam engine by age 19. At age 22, he invented the revolutionary air brake for locomotives. Westinghouse and his team would later pioneer AC current and work with Nikola Tesla.

UNM.name: Unum Group
UNM.fact: 1 in 3 companies of the Fortune 500 offer Unum benefits to their employees.

CNA.name: CNA Financial Corporation
CNA.fact: CNA derives its name from the first letter of three acquired companies: Continental Causality Company, National Fire Insurance Company, and American Casualty Company.

CMPR.name: Cimpress plc
CMPR.fact: Cimpress is a mass-customization company, able to help other thousands of other businesses produce small quantities of printed materials, including promotionals.

AXTA.name: Axalta Coating Systems Ltd.
AXTA.fact: The American company traces its origins to a German firm, which began in 1866 painting carriages. As the automotive industry progressed, the company pivoted toward coating automotive vehicles. The firm now operates in over 120 counties and has more than 100,000 customers.

IOVA.name: Iovance Biotherapeutics, Inc.
IOVA.fact: Iovance Biotherapeutics' late-stage TIL product candidate has the potential to become the first approved one-time cell therapy for a solid tumor cancer.

FERG.name: Ferguson plc
FERG.fact: Ranked among the world leaders in plumbing fixtures, a Ferguson toilet was made famous on the American sitcom "Married With Children" by lead character, Al Bundy - who famously declared "Ferguson. Now there's a man's flush!". The company is also a leader in heating equipment.

KRT.name: Karat Packaging Inc.
KRT.fact: Karat Earth is a plant-based line of eco-friendly containers for the food and beverage industry. Founded in 2004, Karat has received certifications from the Sustainable Forestry Initiative, Compost Manufacturing Alliance, and BPI Compostable.

NOW.name: ServiceNow, Inc.
NOW.fact: ServiceNow was named to the Fortune World's Most Admired Companies list in 2020.

BAC.name: Bank of America Corporation
BAC.fact: By the 1920s, the Bank of Italy was the only statewide bank in California. Along with offices in New York and Italy, and with a vision to one day have financial centers across the country, the bank changed its name to Bank of America in 1930. By 1945, it became the largest bank in the world.

SWX.name: Southwest Gas Holdings, Inc.
SWX.fact: The holding company is over natural gas companies, including Mountain West and Southwest Gas. However, it is also over Centuri, a utility infrastructure services company.

HD.name: The Home Depot, Inc.
HD.fact: Home Depot's signature orange came from the material used for their early signs, which were made from discarded circus tents.

TSBK.name: Timberland Bancorp, Inc.
TSBK.fact: When lumberjacks needed a bank, Timberland answered the call. The bank began in the year 1915, in the booming timber town of Hoquiam. As of 2021, total assets exceed $1 billion.

ACI.name: Albertsons Companies, Inc.
ACI.fact: Albertson's original store was established in 1939 and was destroyed in 1979. However, a brick monument stands in downtown Boise, Idaho commemorating the original store.

FFIV.name: F5, Inc.
FFIV.fact: F5 Network's name was inspired by the 1996 disaster movie Twister. F5 is the fastest, most powerful grade of tornado on the Fujita scale.

FLO.name: Flowers Foods, Inc.
FLO.fact: This baked foods company owns several food brands such as Nature's Own, Dave's Killer Bread, Wonder, Canyon Bakehouse, and more.

AXP.name: American Express Company
AXP.fact: As World War I raged on, the company was appointed an official agent of the British Government. They were to deliver letters, money, and relief parcels to British prisoners of war. Their employees went into camps to cash drafts for both British and French prisoners and arranged for them to receive money from home.

MKC.name: McCormick & Company, Incorporated
MKC.fact: They co-create custom flavors for 10 of the top 10 food and beverage companies, and all top 10 foodservice restaurant chains worldwide.

OVV.name: Ovintiv Inc.
OVV.fact: The company traces its roots back to the 1880s when the Canadian Pacific Railway received compensation for subsurface rights for a large portion of Alberta and Saskatchewan. Those rights would later be spun off to the company's predecessors. Years later, while drilling for water, the staff of Canadian Pacific Railway discovered natural gas.

AMT.name: American Tower Corporation
AMT.fact: In 1998, American Tower parent company American Radio  is sold to CBS/Viacom. Consequently, American Tower is spun off into a separate company. The Company goes public under the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) as AMT.

DOX.name: Amdocs Limited
DOX.fact: Now based in Missouri, this software company was actually founded in Israel.

COTY.name: Coty Inc.
COTY.fact: Coty owns brands that include Burberry, Calvin Klein, Gucci, and Hugo Boss.

SBAC.name: SBA Communications Corporation
SBAC.fact: This company has built over 32,400 wireless towers in three different continents and 14 different markets.

DPZ.name: Domino's Pizza, Inc.
DPZ.fact: Domino's Pizza sells an average of 3 million pizzas per day. Their most popular topping is pepperoni, followed by sausage, bacon, mushrooms, and pineapple.

HBAN.name: Huntington Bancshares Incorporated
HBAN.fact: In 2012, Huntington started displaying old checks that were written by famous individuals. The most notable check was one written by Lincoln to "self" for $800 dated April 13, 1865, the day before his assassination.

AZO.name: AutoZone, Inc.
AZO.fact: In 1981, Auto Shack, before it was named AutoZone, opened an Express Parts Service warehouse in Memphis, Tennessee allowing customers to order thousands of "hard-to-find" parts not stocked in stores. Today, this is known as Vendor Direct Parts (VDP).

LUV.name: Southwest Airlines Co.
LUV.fact: Southwest Airlines wasn't the airline's original name. It was called "Air Southwest" until 1971.

COF.name: Capital One Financial Corporation
COF.fact: Capital One currently has over 62 million cardholders.

HWM.name: Howmet Aerospace Inc.
HWM.fact: Founded in 1888, by Charles Martin Hall (who discovered the process for smelting aluminum) and industrialist Alfred Hunt, Alcoa is one of the world's top 10 producers of aluminum. The company produces primary aluminum, fabricated aluminum, and combined aluminum. Operations include technology, mining, refining, smelting, fabricating, and recycling.

ONTO.name: Onto Innovation Inc.
ONTO.fact: Onto was founded through the merging of Nanometrics and Rudolph Technologies in 2019.

WTW.name: Willis Towers Watson Public Limited Company

TGT.name: Target Corporation
TGT.fact: Target is a company that helps out when disasters strike. It has been known to make its stores available for use as command centers during rescue and relief efforts.

NTNX.name: Nutanix, Inc.
NTNX.fact: The company was founded in 2009 and only four years later the company reached a $1 billion valuation, making it a "unicorn startup"

OGE.name: OGE Energy Corp.
OGE.fact: The energy company was established in 1902 in Oklahoma City, Oklahoma, which is five years before Oklahoma became a state.

EMN.name: Eastman Chemical Company
EMN.fact: The Chemicals from Coal Facility of Eastman Chemical Company was the first in the United States of America to use coal rather than petroleum as a raw material in acetyl chemicals' commercial production.

PSX.name: Phillips 66
PSX.fact: Phillips has a global refining capacity of 2.2 million barrels of crude oil per day.

FWONK.name: Liberty Media Corporation
FWONK.fact: Formula One group holds exclusive commercial rights to the FIA Formula One World Championship. Formula 1 racing is considered the world's most prestigious motor racing competition. The race runs for nine months and spans 23 races in 21 countries across five continents.

MTZ.name: MasTec, Inc.
MTZ.fact: In 1929, two unemployed carpenters wanted to create a construction company that would serve the Florida market and, eventually, the Southeast. With a handshake and mutual trust, the two men got to work.

HCSG.name: Healthcare Services Group, Inc.
HCSG.fact: Provider of housekeeping, laundry, dining, and nutritional services for the healthcare industry.

NTLA.name: Intellia Therapeutics, Inc.
NTLA.fact: One of Intellia's founders, Jennifer Doudna, co-led the development of CRISPR/Cas9. This genome editing tool has contributed to unprecedented scientific research and has revolutionized medical care and treatment.

MSCI.name: MSCI Inc.
MSCI.fact: MSCI's All Country World Index (ACWI) is composed of 2,400 constituents, 11 sectors, and is the industry's accepted gauge of global stock market activity.

EFX.name: Equifax Inc.
EFX.fact: Retail Credit changed its name in 1979 to Equifax Inc., derived from "equitable factual information."

BF-B.name: Brown-Forman Corporation
BF-B.fact: Company founder J. Garvin Brown started it all in 1870 with $5,500 of saved and borrowed money. He was one of the first to sell whiskey in glass bottles instead of barrels.

FSLY.name: Fastly, Inc.
FSLY.fact: Fastly's edge network capacity exceeds 145 Tbps and serves over 800 billion requests daily. That is some serious computing power. With a mean purge time of just 150 ms, it is also quite fast indeed. Major clients include Stripe, Shopify, and The New York Times.

NNN.name: NNN REIT, Inc.
NNN.fact: The real estate company was formed as Golden Corral Realty Corporation to allow the employees of the restaurant chain to have easy access to investing.

REYN.name: Reynolds Consumer Products Inc.
REYN.fact: "HEFTY! HEFTY!" was a commercial campaign that ran in the 1980s by Reynolds to promote its new Hefty trash bags that claimed to be ultra strong.

CVS.name: CVS Health Corp.
CVS.fact: CVS Health Corp was the first pharmacy retailer to stop selling tobacco. This healthy change went into effect on September 3, 2014.

CWT.name: California Water Service Group
CWT.fact: One of the top 3 publicly traded water utilities in the United States of America, CWS serves over 100 communities spread across California, Hawaii, New Mexico, and Washington.

STWD.name: Starwood Property Trust, Inc.
STWD.fact: When this company went public, its IPO was the third-largest REIT in U.S. history.

BLK.name: BlackRock, Inc.
BLK.fact: Amidst the financial crisis, the Head of the Federal Reserve Bank of New York asked BlackRock to analyze Bear Stearns' mortgage-backed securities assets and determine their value.

MAR.name: Marriott International, Inc.
