MAR.fact: Marriott was founded by John Willard Marriott in 1927 when he and his wife, Alice Sheets Marriott, opened a root beer stand in Washington, D.C

SWK.name: Stanley Black & Decker, Inc.
SWK.fact: During World War 2, Stanley Works received the Army-Navy "E" Award for excellence in war production.

AMGN.name: Amgen Inc.
AMGN.fact: Amgen focuses on six therapeutic areas: cardiovascular disease, oncology, bone health, neuroscience, nephrology, and inflammation.

CRUS.name: Cirrus Logic, Inc.
CRUS.fact: Obsessed with great sound, Cirrus Logic is a fabless semiconductor supplier that has made a name for itself providing DSP's for audio experts like Pioneer, Onkyo, Sony, Marantz, and Apple.

MAN.name: ManpowerGroup Inc.
MAN.fact: Two lawyers - Elmer Winter and Aaron Scheinfeld - co-founded Manpower in 1948. They came up with the idea after  they found themselves looking for secretarial work to help with the Wisconsin Supreme Court.

CABO.name: Cable One, Inc.
CABO.fact: The company specializes in cable TV and provides service to roughly 900,000 residential and business customers as of 2020.

YETI.name: YETI Holdings, Inc.
YETI.fact: YETI was founded by two brothers in Texas after they set out to make a cooler that could be used everyday in harsh conditions. They named the company after something they thought would depict a cooler: the Yeti Ice Monster.

DIS.name: The Walt Disney Company
DIS.fact: Walt Disney, the famous filmmaker, had a fascination with trains. It began when, as a teen in Kansas City, he did a brief stint selling newspapers and snacks on trains. During a 1928 train trip, Walt began developing the idea of a character named Mickey Mouse.

BCPC.name: Balchem Corp
BCPC.fact: A group of entrepreneurs, investors, and doctors started Balchem, which was initially housed in a laboratory on the top floor of the Chemists Club in New York City.

STLD.name: Steel Dynamics, Inc.
STLD.fact: As of 2021, the steel company is domestically ranked the third largest producer of carbon steel products.

NUE.name: Nucor Corporation
NUE.fact: In 1905, Ransom E. Olds, creator of the Oldsmobile, had a dispute with stockholders and left his own company  Olds Motor Works. He soon formed REO Motor Company, which evolved into the Nuclear Corporation of America and ultimately, Nucor.

CRL.name: Charles River Laboratories International, Inc.
CRL.fact: In 1947, a young veterinarian purchased one thousand rat cages from a Virginia farm and set up a one-man laboratory in Boston, overlooking the Charles River. Dr. Henry Foster's company is now a leading global provider of pre-clinical and clinical research.

EQH.name: Equitable Holdings, Inc.
EQH.fact: The company was founded in 1859 by Henry Baldwin Hyde. In 1870, he established his headquarters in Manhattan, New York, in what was the tallest building in the United States of America at the time.

SEB.name: Seaboard Corporation
SEB.fact: Otto Bresky purchased his first flour mill in Atchison, Kansas, in 1918. Since then, Seaboard has integrated operations in several industries, becoming #406 on the 2021 Fortune 500 list.

LIN.name: Linde plc
LIN.fact: In October 2018, Praxair and Linde AG came together to create Linde plc, the UK's leading industrial gas and engineering company.

PANW.name: Palo Alto Networks, Inc.
PANW.fact: Palo Alto Networks is a global leader in cybersecurity and firewall technology. The company's history includes having at least 85 Fortune 100 member companies as clients.

TRUP.name: Trupanion, Inc.
TRUP.fact: In Trupanion's first 20 years, the company celebrated 500,000 insured pets in North America and over $1 billion in paid claims on behalf of its members.

H.name: Hyatt Hotels Corporation
H.fact: The multinational juggernaut in the hospitality industry has its roots going back to a motel near the Los Angeles International Airport.

PRPL.name: Purple Innovation, Inc.
PRPL.fact: Mattresses, pillows, cushions, sheets... Purple Innovation makes them all. The company was founded by rocket scientist brothers, Terry and Tony Pearce, in 1989 - who would go on to bring their proprietary GelFlex Grid technology to the world of sleep science.

CRNC.name: Cerence Inc.
CRNC.fact: Cerence is the world's leading provider of automotive assistants and there are more than 450 million cars with Cerence technology, which is 1 in every 2 cars in the world.

WELL.name: Welltower Inc.
WELL.fact: Welltower, renamed in 2015, was originally called Health Care Fund. The company owned two nursing facilities with a combined value of under $800,000.

ITT.name: ITT Inc.
ITT.fact: This manufacturing firm was established by two brothers as a telephone company in 1920. It has since become a conglomerate of diversified industries including aerospace, transportation, energy, and industrials.

AEE.name: Ameren Corporation
AEE.fact: The company owns 3,300 miles of natural gas transmission and distribution mains in Missouri.

CGNX.name: Cognex Corporation
CGNX.fact: This company was founded by Robert J. Shillman, a lecturer in human visual perception at MIT, along with two MIT graduate students.

ZM.name: Zoom Communications, Inc.
ZM.fact: Thanks, in part, to the COVID-19 pandemic, Zoom's easy to use video-conferencing grew from 10 million daily meeting participants (2019) to over 300 million (2021).

FLYW.name: Flywire Corp
FLYW.fact: Flywire represents over 40 nationalities and covers more than 249 countries and territories and supports over 140 currencies.

TPL.name: Texas Pacific Land Corporation
TPL.fact: The company was created through a federal charter for the construction of a transcontinental railroad from Texas to California. Ten years later in 1881, T&P had completed 972 miles of track across 3.5 million acres of land in Texas.

WD.name: Walker & Dunlop, Inc.
WD.fact: Walker & Dunlop recorded $68 billion in total transactions, making it the third multifamily capital provider in 2021.

HRI.name: Herc Holdings Inc.
HRI.fact: With more than 50 years of equipment rental expertise, Herc is considered one of the largest rental equipment companies in North America.

SNPS.name: Synopsys, Inc.
SNPS.fact: The Synopsys ImageNet Challenge is a high-stakes annual competition that attempts to replicate the human brain through artificial intelligence.

SITM.name: SiTime Corporation
SITM.fact: SiTime has shipped over 2 billion timing devices.

FN.name: Fabrinet
FN.fact: One of Thailand’s top employers, Fabrinet’s two campuses are located just outside of Bangkok, less than an hour’s drive from the international airport. Fabrinet’s well-established operations take prime advantage of Asia-located suppliers to drive reductions in material cost.

VSAT.name: Viasat, Inc.
VSAT.fact: With satellite services spanning 1,400+ commercial aircraft and approximately 590k total U.S. fixed broadband subscribers, it comes as no surprise that CNET's awarded Viasat with the 20221 Best Satellite Provider for U.S. rural internet services.

DECK.name: Deckers Outdoor Corporation
DECK.fact: Deckers owns the worldwide fashion footwear brand, Ugg. They must have a poster of Tom Brady somewhere…

LECO.name: Lincoln Electric Holdings, Inc.
LECO.fact: The manufacturing company was founded in 1895 by John Lincoln who established the company for only $200. In 1917, the Lincoln Electric Welding School was established to promote the education of the welding industry and has since instructed over 150,000 men and women.

PG.name: The Procter & Gamble Company
PG.fact: During the American Civil War, the company had contracts with the Union Army, supplying them with soap and candles.

ULTA.name: Ulta Beauty, Inc.
ULTA.fact: According to the Washington Post, "about 77% of Ulta shoppers own more than 11 lipsticks, and 68% own more than two curling irons."

WFC.name: Wells Fargo & Company
WFC.fact: The company operates 12 museums, most known as a Wells Fargo History Museum. Displays include original stagecoaches, photographs, gold nuggets and mining artifacts, the Pony Express, telegraph equipment and historic bank artifacts.

UPST.name: Upstart Holdings, Inc.
UPST.fact: Upstart offers an AI-powered lending platform to help banks and credit unions provide consumer loans. The company utilizes proprietary methods to assess credit risk.

HAE.name: Haemonetics Corporation
HAE.fact: Blood and plasma supplies and services comprise the core business of Haemonetics. In Greek mythology, Haemon was the son of Creon and Eurydice, famous for a bloody and self-inflticed death.

PBI.name: Pitney Bowes Inc.
PBI.fact: In business for over 100 years, Pitney Bowes simplifies sending of mail and parcels for over 90% of Fortune 500 companies, making it a leading digital mailroom service provider. Active in e-commerce, the firm is also the #1 Parcel Return solution in the United States of America.

CERT.name: Certara, Inc.
CERT.fact: Certara produced over 250 global regulatory and health authority submissions and delivered in the past 4 years.

CZR.name: Caesars Entertainment, Inc.
CZR.fact: Caesar's Palace hotel and casino has featured a who's who of famous performers over the years, including the likes of Frank Sinatra, Ella Fitzgerald, Dean Martin, Sammy Davis Jr. Count Basie, Bette Midler, Elton John, Shania Twain, and Cher. And that's just the short list...

FHB.name: First Hawaiian, Inc.
FHB.fact: Founded in 1858, First Hawaiian is Hawaii's oldest and largest financial institution.

HQY.name: HealthEquity, Inc.
HQY.fact: The company has served over 14 million members, but that’s not all. HealthEquity plans to make HSAs more common than 401(k)s by 2030.

MXL.name: MaxLinear, Inc.
MXL.fact: MaxLinear was founded by eight engineers from very diverse backgrounds. These individuals, unique in their own way, came together to create an S&P 600 Component.

HAIN.name: The Hain Celestial Group, Inc.
HAIN.fact: Hain Celestial has 14 #1 brands. Some of its brands include ParmCrisps, Garden Veggie Straws, Thinsters, and more.

CG.name: The Carlyle Group Inc.
CG.fact: Carlyle Group is a global investment firm with over $260 billion in assets, as of 2021.

UNF.name: UniFirst Corporation
UNF.fact: UniFirst started its operations in a converted horse barn in Boston, MA, in 1936. It started with cleaning the coveralls of workers in factories and other blue-collar workers. The company has grown to become one of North America's largest workwear and textile service companies, supplying more than 2 million workers with clean uniforms each workday.

FIVE.name: Five Below, Inc.
FIVE.fact: Five Below offers most of its products at a price of about five dollars (or below).

APH.name: Amphenol Corporation
APH.fact: Amphenol is a world leader in designing, manufacturing, and supplying high-performance interconnect systems for harsh environment military applications.

FMC.name: FMC Corporation
FMC.fact: FMC's history includes production of firetruck pumps, as well as military equipment.

ORI.name: Old Republic International Corporation
ORI.fact: This corporation ranks in the top three of the title insurance industry.

OMF.name: OneMain Holdings, Inc.
OMF.fact: This financial services company was originally a subsidiary of Citigroup, but after the 2008 financial crisis, the company was reorganized and renamed OneMain Financial.

SPOT.name: Spotify Technology S.A.
SPOT.fact: Spotify offers streaming music, podcasts, and other audio content. Since its founding in 2006, it has grown to roughly half a billion total users. As of 2022, Ed Sheeran holds the record for most songs with over 1 billion streams (10).

COHR.name: Coherent, Inc.
COHR.fact: Six engineers shared a dream of starting a business together that would change fiber laser equipment forever. The founders gathered $10,000 with their own money and released the first commercially-available carbon dioxide laser in the same year. Within the first year, Coherent did $250,000 in sales.

MSM.name: MSC Industrial Direct Co., Inc.
MSM.fact: MSC is famous for publishing "The Big Book," a catalog that describes in detail the company's 1+ million products in a roughly 3,000-page book.

DELL.name: Dell Technologies Inc.
DELL.fact: Founder Michael Dell's first computer was reportedly an Apple II. He later made a business of building and upgrading computers in his college dorm-room, even winning some government contracts in his home state of Texas.

GPC.name: Genuine Parts Company
GPC.fact: In North America, more than 500,000 parts are sold under the NAPA brand name as a subsidiary of Genuine Parts, and is widely recognized for the outstanding quality of their products.

C.name: Citigroup Inc.
C.fact: During the war of 1812, the United States of America' currency and treasury bills were losing value, trade was languishing, and businesses were failing. In mid-July, City Bank of New York appointed a committee of directors to "make proper arrangements for removing the books, cash, etc., belonging to the bank, in case of the invasion of the city by the enemy."

SMG.name: The Scotts Miracle-Gro Company
SMG.fact: In 1868, a Civil War veteran, Orlando Scott, opened a hardware store where he sold weed-free seed to local farmers. Soon after he refined his product, he sold his product to homeowners, which was the first time anyone developed and sold seeds to the open market.

FWRD.name: Forward Air Corporation
FWRD.fact: Forward Air is a leading provider of ground transportation and logistics.

ALKS.name: Alkermes plc
ALKS.fact: The biotech company has multiple products that meet unmet central nervous system diseases such as serious mental illness, addiction, and cancer.

HRB.name: H&R Block, Inc.
HRB.fact: Two brothers, Henry and Richard Bloch founded H&R Block in 1955. The company has since prepared more than 800 million tax returns worldwide.

SAIC.name: Science Applications International Corporation
SAIC.fact: SAIC provides the U.S. Army, Navy, Air Force, and Marine Corps with cutting-edge warfighting technologies.

ATO.name: Atmos Energy Corporation
ATO.fact: Atmos Energy pledged to reduce their methane emissions in their natural gas distribution systems by 50% from 2017 to 2035.

SKYW.name: SkyWest, Inc.
SKYW.fact: With 620+ aircraft, SkyWest is a regional airline. It also leases aircraft and spare engines. The company was founded in 1972.

GPN.name: Global Payments Inc.
GPN.fact: Global Payments has designed payment solutions for over 2.5 million businesses!

CNO.name: CNO Financial Group, Inc.
CNO.fact: CNO ranks among the largest financial services companies headquarted within Indiana. The company specializes in insurance, with subsidiaries offering life insurance, supplemental health insurance, and annuity products to more than 4 million customers.

MTH.name: Meritage Homes Corporation
MTH.fact: Over its first 36 years in the industry, Meritage Homes delivered well over 145,000 homes.

SYNA.name: Synaptics Incorporated
SYNA.fact: If you've used a touchscreen, trackpad or fingerprint sensor there's a good chance you've used a Synaptics technology. The company's history includes use of its products in various Apple devices and Google Chromebooks, among others.

LKQ.name: LKQ Corporation
LKQ.fact: LKQ is the largest recycler of automobiles in the world. 95% of the materials from end of life vehicles is recycled as opposed to being in a landfill.

GEN.name: Gen Digital Inc.
GEN.fact: Formerly known as Norton LifeLock, a cybersecurity company founded by Peter Norton in 1982, with $30,000 and an IBM computer. By 1988, Norton was named Entrepreneur of the Year by Arthur Young & Co. and Venture magazine.

ADC.name: Agree Realty Corporation
ADC.fact: As of March 2022, Agree Realty owned and operated a portfolio of 1,510 properties with roughly 31 million square feet of gross leasable space.

TRMB.name: Trimble Inc.
TRMB.fact: In 1990, Trimble was the first company that focused on GPS solutions. Companies that followed include Garmin, Motorola, and Raymarine.

CNM.name: Core & Main, Inc.
CNM.fact: Core & Main was built on the legacy of 80+ companies, making it a leading distributor of water, sewer, storm drain, and fire protection products in the United States of America.

IFF.name: International Flavors & Fragrances Inc.
IFF.fact: IFF had a goal to reduce GHG emissions intensity by 25%. They actually reduced it by 33.8%.

CPF.name: Central Pacific Financial Corp.
CPF.fact: Founded by Koichi Iida in 1954, Central Pacific Financial's early backers included the Japanese conglomerate, Sumitomo.

TER.name: Teradyne, Inc.
TER.fact: Teradyne has the capability of testing the memory of your computers.

GILD.name: Gilead Sciences, Inc.
GILD.fact: The Gilead COMPASS (COMmitment to Partnership in Addressing HIV/AIDS in Southern States) Initiative is a $100 million, 10-year commitment to help address HIV/AIDS in the South  home to about 44 percent of people living with AIDS in the U.S..

NSC.name: Norfolk Southern Corporation
NSC.fact: Committed to a reforestation project to plant 6 million trees.

BIIB.name: Biogen Inc.
BIIB.fact: Biogen has focused its R&D efforts on the discovery and development of treatments for patients with high unmet medical needs in the areas of neurology, hematology and immunology.

DRI.name: Darden Restaurants, Inc.
DRI.fact: Darden Restaurants owns Olive Garden, LongHorn Steakhouse, Bahama Breeze, Seasons 52 Yard House, Cheddars, and used to own Red Lobster.

WDAY.name: Workday, Inc.
WDAY.fact: Workday's Enterprise Management Cloud helps business manage and optimize human resources.

PGR.name: The Progressive Corporation
PGR.fact: Progressive was the first to let customers name their own price for insurance, with the Name Your Price tool (2009).

BMRN.name: BioMarin Pharmaceutical Inc.
BMRN.fact: BioMarin was the first company to provide therapeutics for mucopolysaccharidosis and phenylketonuria.

WMB.name: The Williams Companies, Inc.
WMB.fact: Williams traces its history to 1908, when brothers S. Miller Williams, Jr. and David R. Williams were working for a construction contractor who had an order to pave sidewalks in Fort Smith, Arkansas.

OSBC.name: Old Second Bancorp, Inc.
OSBC.fact: Old Second engages in community banking and trust services, primarily in the state of Illinois.

CEVA.name: CEVA, Inc.
CEVA.fact: CEVA, Inc. specializes in ultra-low-power digital signal processors (DSP's), AI processors, wireless platforms, and IoT. The company licenses its technology to more than 400 of the world's leading semiconductor companies. Over 13 billion CEVA-powered chips have been sent forth into the world.

SEIC.name: SEI Investments Company
SEIC.fact: As of 2022, the financial institution had $1.3 trillion in assets under management and assets under administration.

MLI.name: Mueller Industries, Inc.
MLI.fact: Founded in 1917, Mueller Industries is engaged in copper and copper alloy manufacturing, with products directed at both B2B and consumer customers.

AMH.name: American Homes 4 Rent
AMH.fact: As of 2022, the company owned 52,552 homes. Most of these residential homes are located in Atlanta, Georgia, Dallas-Fort Worth, Texas, and Charlotte, North Carolina.

AMWL.name: American Well Corporation
AMWL.fact: A telemedicine firm (that has nothing to do with drilling), Amwell connects doctors and patients via its secure video service.

ISRG.name: Intuitive Surgical, Inc.
ISRG.fact: The da Vinci Surgical System was one of the first robotic-assisted, minimally invasive surgical systems cleared by the FDA. Today, a family of da Vinci systems and technologies is used by surgeons in all 50 U.S. states and 66 countries around the world.

PFE.name: Pfizer Inc.
PFE.fact: Pfizer made most of the penicillin given to the Allied forces that stormed Normandy on D-Day during World War II. Their leadership in tough times continues, as they were the first company to be approved for emergency vaccine production by the FDA, in December 2020.

BYD.name: Boyd Gaming Corporation
BYD.fact: Sam Boyd, the co-founder of Boyd Gaming with his son, started his career in Las Vegas, Nevada as a dealer. He simply worked his way up promotion by promotion and made the right financial moves. The father-son duo created a juggernaut in the gambling, hotel, and entertainment industry by operating over 25 properties with more than 10,000 hotel rooms.

PSFE.name: Paysafe Limited
PSFE.fact: In 2019, the security company managed annualized transactional volume of over $98bn.

XYL.name: Xylem Inc.
XYL.fact: As a water technology provider, Xylem has a responsibility to the environment and plans on reducing its impact on the planet. They plan to do this by reducing water use in industrial facilities by 25% by 2019, reducing GHG emissions intensity by 20% by 2019, and reducing waste to landfill rates by 20% by 2019.

FMNB.name: Farmers National Banc Corp.
FMNB.fact: Farmers was founded on February 19, 1887. Alexander Dickson, a former school teacher, Civil War captain and Treasurer of Mahoning County, was named the bank's president at its first charter meeting. On the bank's first day of business, a total of $170 was deposited from a tavern keeper, barber, school master, two tailors and a housewife.

FUL.name: H.B. Fuller Company
FUL.fact: H.B. Fuller Company was founded in 1887, you guessed it, by Harvey Benjamin Fuller. The company's legacy began with the introduction of Fuller's Premium Liquid Fish Glue, which was considered to be able to "cement everything." Although it was the first, H.B. Fuller Company was not going to stop its innovative spirit with the Liquid Fish Glue, in fact, Fisher was just getting started.

FIGS.name: FIGS, Inc.
FIGS.fact: Heather Hasson, the Co-CEO and Co-Founder of Figs came up with the idea after grabbing coffee with a friend and nurse practitioner. Heather could not believe that her friend would work 16-hour shifts in boxy, scratchy, and uncomfortable clothing. So, she set out to change that by using technically advanced apparel to revolutionize healthcare professional's uniforms.

ROK.name: Rockwell Automation, Inc.
ROK.fact: For its Milwaukee headquarters, Rockwell built the largest four-sided clock in the world (each side nearly twice as large as London's "Big Ben"). Also nicknamed "The Polish Moon", it sits atop the building's 280-ft tall Allen-Bradley clock tower.

SNA.name: Snap-on Incorporated
SNA.fact: Snap-on has paid consecutive quarterly cash dividends without interruption or reduction, since 1939 - one of the best streaks of dividend payment in stock market history.

BKR.name: Baker Hughes Company
BKR.fact: In January of 2019, Baker Hughes made an announcement that they plan to reduce Scope 1 and 2 operating emissions by 50% by 2030 and net zero emissions by 2050.

DHR.name: Danaher Corporation
DHR.fact: Danaher takes its' name from a tributary of the South Fork Flat Head River in western Montana.

TT.name: Trane Technologies plc
TT.fact: In the 1920s, Ingersoll Rand supplied diesel engines for locomotives built by both General Electric and ALCO.

DKNG.name: DraftKings Inc.
DKNG.fact: The three founders of DraftKings, Robins, Liberman, and Kalish, launched their company from a spare bedroom of an apartment in Watertown, Massachusetts.

M.name: Macy's, Inc.
M.fact: Rowland Hussey Macy adopted a big red star as the symbol of his brand in the mid 1800s, which has continued as the retailer's iconic symbol to this day. In the first day of sales, the company did $11.06, but after the first year, the company grossed roughly $85,000.

FDX.name: FedEx Corporation
FDX.fact: In fiscal year 2020, FedEx Express delivered roughly 6 million packages daily.

JJSF.name: J&J Snack Foods Corp.
JJSF.fact: Founded in 1971, J&J Snack Foods is one of the largest soft pretzel makers in the world. The company also excels at funnel cakes, churros, slushies, cookies, and muffins - among many other delicious products.

CFG.name: Citizens Financial Group, Inc.
CFG.fact: Citizens Bank is the 13th largest retail bank in the United States of America.

FNB.name: F.N.B. Corporation
FNB.fact: This Pittsburgh-based bank was founded in 1864 and remained in a single office that withstood both World Wars and the Great Depression. Like many success stories that endured those extremely difficult times, F.N.B.'s legacy was just beginning. From total assets of approximately $2 million in 1946, the company has grown to more than $40 billion in total assets as of 2022.

BBY.name: Best Buy Co., Inc.
BBY.fact: Best Buy has helped customers recycle more than 2 billion pounds of electronics and appliances since 2009. That makes Best Buy the largest retail collector of e-waste in the United States of America.

LNT.name: Alliant Energy Corporation
LNT.fact: By 2026, Alliant forecasts a 40% reduction of their 2005 carbon emissions ahead of the Wisconsin 2030 deadline.

BXP.name: BXP, Inc.
BXP.fact: Boston Properties holds a superior track record in developing premium Central Business District office buildings, suburban office centers, and build-to-suit projects for the U.S. government and various creditworthy tenants.

ASAN.name: Asana, Inc.
ASAN.fact: One of Asana's cofounders, Dustin Moskovitz, had previously helped launch another successful company - Facebook - which, according to Forbes, made him the youngest self-made billionaire in history. Along with ex-Facebook engineer, Justin Rosenstein, they created Asana to help teams organize, track, and manage work.

SIRI.name: Sirius XM Holdings Inc.
SIRI.fact: Perhaps the world's best-known satellite radio operator, Sirius XM famously has paid media icon, Howard Stern, over $100 million per year.

OTTR.name: Otter Tail Corporation
OTTR.fact: Otter Tail is an energy company serving over 400 towns and 14 municipal utilities. Founded in 1907, its has traditionaly served customers in Minnesota, North Dakota, and South Dakota.

DTM.name: DT Midstream, Inc.
DTM.fact: DT is among the first midstream companies to implement a program set to achieve net zero greenhouse gas emissions by 2050.

ARE.name: Alexandria Real Estate Equities, Inc.
ARE.fact: In 2002, Alexandria launched its first proprietary product, the Science Hotel, which was designed for leading early-stage life science companies.

AVGO.name: Broadcom Inc.
AVGO.fact: In the 1970s, Broadcom introduced the first fiber optic transmitters and receivers for data communications.

KMB.name: Kimberly-Clark Corporation
KMB.fact: Kleenex, one of Kimberly-Clark's most famous brands, was originally developed during World War I as crepe paper filtration used in gas masks.

THO.name: Thor Industries, Inc.
THO.fact: "Thor" was the product of combining the first two letters from the last names of the two founders: Wade Thompson and Peter Orthwein. It also sounds cool.

ADT.name: ADT Inc.
ADT.fact: ADT was formed after Edward Calahan was inspired to create an alarm system after his home was broken into. He connected 50 of his neighbors to a central station so that people could be warned of danger. Then in 1874, many small telegraph delivery companies formed American District Telegraph.

MCK.name: McKesson Corporation
MCK.fact: McKesson operated the Mosswood Wine Company from 1978 until 1987, when the division was sold to maintain their focus on pharmaceuticals.

PAG.name: Penske Automotive Group, Inc.
PAG.fact: In 1990, the automotive company was acquired by Penske Corporation. Now with over 27,000 employees, the company is a member of the Fortune 500 and the Russell 1000.

ASO.name: Academy Sports and Outdoors, Inc.
ASO.fact: In 1938, the first Academy store was opened as a tire shop. Then it turned into a military surplus store, and then it later turned into the sports and outdoor store we know today.

NGVC.name: Natural Grocers by Vitamin Cottage, Inc.

JAZZ.name: Jazz Pharmaceuticals plc
JAZZ.fact: The pharmaceutical company's biggest product is the FDA approved Xyrem. In 2017, the net sales of the drug hit $1.87 billion.

MAA.name: Mid-America Apartment Communities, Inc.
MAA.fact: As of September 30, 2018, MAA owned or had ownership interest in 101,441 homes.

STZ.name: Constellation Brands, Inc.
STZ.fact: This company is known for being the number one premium wine producer in the world.

PZZA.name: Papa John's International, Inc.
PZZA.fact: "Papa" John Schnatter began his journey in the pizza business by using a broom closet in the back of his father's tavern. John was so intent on making his dream a reality that he sold his 1971 Camaro Z28 to invest in the company. After years of expansion and growth, he bought that car back for $250,000. Papa John's also benefitted from the new world of digital currency. On May 22, 2010, a trade was made: 10,000 bitcoins for two large Papa John's pizzas. May 22nd is now celebrated annually by individuals as "Bitcoin Pizza Day."

JEF.name: Jefferies Financial Group Inc.
JEF.fact: This financial group is listed on the Fortune 1000 and made over $8 billion in 2021.

MP.name: MP Materials Corp.
MP.fact: From 1965 to 1995, Mountain Pass produced the majority of global rare earth materials. So infamous, it was coined the "Mountain Pass Era."

MOH.name: Molina Healthcare, Inc.
MOH.fact: David Molina founded the company in 1980 when he noticed the lowest-income individuals were getting turned away by doctors because they would not accept Medi-Cal. He pledged to establish a clinic with the goal that the lowest-income patients would be treated, even if they did not have the sufficient funds to pay for the treatment.

ALLY.name: Ally Financial Inc.
ALLY.fact: General Motors founded the General Motors Acceptance Corporation to provide financing for automotive customers. Nearly a century later, GMAC re-branded as the Ally company, evolving into what it is today.

LAD.name: Lithia Motors, Inc.
LAD.fact: Lithia Motors was founded in 1946 as a Chrysler/Plymouth/Dodge dealership in Oregon. Today, the company owns over 250 domestic and foreign car dealerships in the U.S. and Canada, with 38 brands and more than 50,000 vehicles available at any given time.

WHR.name: Whirlpool Corporation
WHR.fact: In 1962, the company's research laboratories won a contract from NASA to develop the food and waste management system for Project Gemini.

HCC.name: Warrior Met Coal, Inc.
HCC.fact: One of Alabama's largest coal mine operators, Warrior Met supplies non-thermal metallurgical coal to help power blast furnances for the global steel industry. Clients range into Europe, South America, and Asia.

PH.name: Parker-Hannifin Corporation
PH.fact: Parker's Outdoor Energy Storage PCS (power conversion system) is designed for extreme outdoor environments. It also has a small footprint.

CRBU.name: Caribou Biosciences, Inc.
CRBU.fact: Caribou Biosciences is a clinical stage company that seeks to develop therapies to treat terrible diseases by using genome-edited cells.

RHP.name: Ryman Hospitality Properties, Inc.
RHP.fact: RHP's core holding represents some of the largest convention centers and resorts in prime real estate areas that have a combined total of 10,000+ rooms and operate more than 2.8 million square feet of total indoor and outdoor meeting space.

MET.name: MetLife, Inc.
MET.fact: The predecessor company to MetLife began in 1863 when a group of New York City businessmen raised $100,000 to found the National Union Life and Limb Insurance Company. The company insured Civil War sailors and soldiers against disabilities due to wartime wounds, accidents, and sickness

SHOO.name: Steven Madden, Ltd.
SHOO.fact: From humble beginnings and a modest investment of $1,100, Steve Madden sold shoes out of the trunk of his car. Through innovation and inspiration, the company has now exceeded billions of dollars in revenue for years.

GPK.name: Graphic Packaging Holding Company
GPK.fact: This packaging company's history extends more than 100 years and has evolved with the times. With products that emphasize renewable, recycled, and recycled materials, for many Fortune 500 companies.

PYPL.name: PayPal Holdings, Inc.
PYPL.fact: PayPal owns social P2P mobile payment giant Venmo. The platform, a favorite among millennials, processed $6.8 billion worth of payments in the first-quarter, which was up 114% year-over-year.

GGG.name: Graco Inc.
GGG.fact: in 1926, Russell Gray and his brother Leil recognized a need for an air-powered grease gun that would not malfunction due to the cold. In the first several years of WWII, the company reached annual sales of $1 million because of the necessity for defense-based lubrication.

HAL.name: Halliburton Company
HAL.fact: Halliburton's fascinating and proud history reveals a continuous focus on innovation and expansion that began with the company's founder, Erle P. Halliburton. After borrowing a wagon, a team of mules and a pump, he built a wooden mixing box and started an oil well cementing business in Duncan, Oklahoma.

ALGN.name: Align Technology, Inc.
ALGN.fact: The Invisalign system is the most advanced clear aligner system in the world, trusted by more than 9.0 million people worldwide to improve their smiles.

EXR.name: Extra Space Storage Inc.
EXR.fact: Extra Space Storage is the largest third-party management company in the U.S.

GVA.name: Granite Construction Incorporated
GVA.fact: Founded in 1922, Granite Construction is one of the largest diversified construction and construction materials companies in the United States of America. The company specializes in complex infrastructure projects, including federal contracts.

ERIE.name: Erie Indemnity Company
ERIE.fact: ERIE was founded in 1925, by two insurance salesmen who decided to quit their jobs and start their own company. The salesmen, H.O. Hirt and O.G. Crawford, believed auto insurance could be a great business, as it was becoming possible for more and more Americans to afford cars. Pitching a hand-written business plan, the two founders were able to raise $31,000 in less than four months and launch ERIE.

ROKU.name: Roku, Inc.
ROKU.fact: Roku, LLC was founded in 2002 by Anthony Wood, a very determined tech entrepreneur. Wood had previously started a Tivo competitor, called ReplayTV - but it failed. Undeterred, he ended up working on a set-top-box for Netflix, codename: "Project: Griffin". Just weeks before launch, Netflix CEO, Reed Hastings, got cold feet. Wondering, "Will Apple still use Netflix if we build our own box?", Roku was spun-off from Netflix and incorporated. By 2021, the little spin-off had grown to a market cap in excess of $40 billion.

VOYA.name: Voya Financial, Inc.
VOYA.fact: As of 2022, this financial health, wealth, and investment company serves the needs of 14.3 million individuals.

WAT.name: Waters Corporation
WAT.fact: 60+ years in business, Waters is now one of largest companies in the analytical instruments industry, supporting scientists working in thousands of laboratories around the world.

XEL.name: Xcel Energy Inc.
XEL.fact: Insperity started with two people sharing a one-room office, but has grown to a company with more than 70 offices across the Unites States.

RHI.name: Robert Half Inc.
RHI.fact: Robert Half International is the world's largest specialized staffing firm.

EL.name: The Estée Lauder Companies Inc.
EL.fact: Aramis, launched by the company in 1963, was the first prestige men's fragrance to be sold in department stores.

BBWI.name: Bath & Body Works, Inc.
BBWI.fact: This company's flagship brand is Bath and Body Works. L Brands was the parent company of Victoria's Secret until 2021.

DG.name: Dollar General Corporation
DG.fact: 75% of Americans are currently within 5 miles of a Dollar General store.

NTAP.name: NetApp, Inc.
NTAP.fact: With NetApp technology, DreamWorks quickly and efficiently manages the massive amounts of data needed to make its animated films come to life.

DHI.name: D.R. Horton, Inc.
DHI.fact: D.R. Horton has been the largest homebuilder by volume in the United States of America since 2002.

YUM.name: Yum! Brands, Inc.
YUM.fact: Outside the United States of America in 2006, Yum's system opened about three new restaurants each day of the year making it one of the fastest growing retailers in the world.

NDAQ.name: Nasdaq, Inc.
NDAQ.fact: Despite its name, the Nasdaq 100 has more than 100 stocks in its index.

SHLS.name: Shoals Technologies Group, Inc.
SHLS.fact: As of 2022, Shoals had 20 US patents for a wide variety of systems and accessories.

LAUR.name: Laureate Education, Inc.
LAUR.fact: Based in Miami, Laureate Education operates a network of 25 higher education institutions focused on Latin America, primarily in Mexico and Peru.

SSTK.name: Shutterstock, Inc.
SSTK.fact: Spanning 150+ countries, Shutterstock celebrated over 1 billion images, video clips, and music tracks downloaded.

GWRS.name: Global Water Resources, Inc.
GWRS.fact: "Total Water Management" is the focus of Global Water Resources, which owns 17 water and wastewater utilities - primarily in the Phoenix MSA.

VMC.name: Vulcan Materials Company
VMC.fact: In 1957, Vulcan Materials Company asked stockholders to approve a merger involving nine companies at the same time Union Chemicals, Lambert Brothers, and seven other related corporations. Fortune Magazine observed that the prospectus issued for the transaction was one of the most complex ever printed.

TDY.name: Teledyne Technologies Incorporated
TDY.fact: The name "Teledyne" means "distant force" or "power from afar".

DVN.name: Devon Energy Corporation
DVN.fact: In 1950, Devon co-founder John Nichols created the first public oil and gas drilling fund registered with the SEC.

RF.name: Regions Financial Corporation
RF.fact: All three of its original banks weathered economic crisis in their early years, including the 1929 stock market crash and the Great Depression. It is remarkable that all three banks survived the Depression as four out of every 10 banks in Alabama failed during that time.

IP.name: International Paper Company
IP.fact: More than 90 percent of International Papers fiber supply in the United States of America comes from privately owned forests, most of which are small and family-owned.

EXLS.name: ExlService Holdings, Inc.
EXLS.fact: With 39,000+ professionals, EXL serves over 700 clients.

STT.name: State Street Corporation
STT.fact: State Street is responsible for approximately 10% of the world's financial assets.

L.name: Loews Corporation
L.fact: CCC, a company that Loews finances, states that 97% of its products are recyclable.

UAL.name: United Airlines Holdings, Inc.
UAL.fact: United Boeing 247s flew the same route on the Main Line that settlers followed to the West. The 247 could cross North America in a single night and was the first modern airline

ARES.name: Ares Management Corporation
ARES.fact: Ares is one of the largest alternative asset management firms in the world, with $334 billion in assets under management, as of 2022.

TXT.name: Textron Inc.
TXT.fact: Textron's subsidiary, Bell Helicopter, was pivotal in the Vietnam war. The Army embraced Bell's AH-1 Cobra because of its slim profile and lightweight plexiglass canopy.

ARRY.name: Array Technologies, Inc.
ARRY.fact: Array Technologies makes precision solar tracking and ground-mounting systems for the solar power industry. This enables vast panel banks of solar farms to gradually track the sun's movements throughout the day, enabling much more efficient power generation.

SBUX.name: Starbucks Corporation
SBUX.fact: Did you know Santa Fe Springs, California has the highest concentration of Starbucks locations on the planet? 560 stores within a 25 mile radius.

NXPI.name: NXP Semiconductors N.V.
NXPI.fact: In terms of research and development, NXP has around 11,200 engineers operating in 23 countries and over 9,000 patents issued or pending.

TMUS.name: T-Mobile US, Inc.
TMUS.fact: T-Mobile's former CEO, John Legere, once tried to crash a party AT&T was throwing in 2014. He was promptly throw out and escorted off the premises. He was quoted saying, "I just wanted to hear Macklemore", who at the time was a hit artist who sang Thrift Shop, Glorious, and Summer Days.

NTRS.name: Northern Trust Corporation
NTRS.fact: During its history of over 130 years, the company has only had 10 chief executive officers.

WWW.name: Wolverine World Wide, Inc.
WWW.fact: Wolverine is the parent company of footwear brands such as Merrell, Saucony, Sperry, Keds, and Hush Puppies.

WTFC.name: Wintrust Financial Corporation
WTFC.fact: Wintrust prides itself in not being just another bank. So, in 1991, Ed Wehmer started a bank in Chicago that would give a hospitable and local touch that many banks forgot about.

O.name: Realty Income Corporation
O.fact: Realty pays out 90% of its taxable income to shareholders. Wow!

KTB.name: Kontoor Brands, Inc.
KTB.fact: Leaders in denim, Kontoor owns the Lee, Wrangler, and Rock &  Republic brands. It also operate VF Outlet factory stores.

UHAL.name: U-Haul Holding Company
UHAL.fact: AMERCO is the parent company of U-Haul. The "do-it-yourself" company originated post-WWII when many families needed a one-way relocation of their valuables. Leonard Shoen and his wife acted on this entrepreneurial instinct and established a new industry.

GBCI.name: Glacier Bancorp, Inc.
GBCI.fact: Based just south of Glacier National Park, this bank holding company encompasses numerous smaller bank brands throughout the Rocky Mountain states. Total assets exceed $25 billion.

GIS.name: General Mills, Inc.
GIS.fact: From 1965 to 1985, this company (best known for cereal) operated a toy division that included such businesses as Parker Brothers, Play-Doh, Kenner and Lionel Trains. Toys developed under General Mills ownership include the Nerf ball, Care Bears, Paint-by-Numbers and the Betty Crocker Easy Bake Oven.

DUOL.name: Duolingo, Inc.
DUOL.fact: With over 500 million total users, Duolingo is the most downloaded education app in the world. Company cofounders, Luis von Ahn and Severin Hacker, met at Carnegie Mellon University and would go on to ring the NASDAQ's opening bell for Duolingo's IPO on July 28, 2021. The stock surged over 30% in its first day, making it one of the most successful IPO's of the year.

BWA.name: BorgWarner Inc.
BWA.fact: In 2018, BorgWarner won a PACE Award for its groundbreaking S-wind wire forming process for electric motors and alternators. This gave the ability to produce smaller, more powerful high-voltage electric motors on a mass scale to drive growth in the hybrid and electric vehicle market.

CAR.name: Avis Budget Group, Inc.
CAR.fact: In 1946, Warren Avis found Avis when he opened the first car rental business at an airport. As of 2022, the company has a fleet of 600,000 vehicles in 11,000 rental locations across 180 countries.

VST.name: Vistra Corp.
VST.fact: The energy and power generation company contains the largest battery energy storage system in the world as of 2021.

SLAB.name: Silicon Laboratories Inc.
SLAB.fact: Three friends who were enjoying an after-work happy hour discussed the pros and cons of starting their own business. One of the guys suggested that they should flip a coin - heads, thery start it and tails they don't. The coin landed on heads and Nav Sooch, Jeff Scott, and Dave Welland founded a company that would make hundreds of millions in revenue annually.

GOOGL.name: Alphabet Inc.
GOOGL.fact: Part of the reason Alphabet was named so was because its founders liked the symbolism. In finance, "alpha" represents investment return above benchmark - so the company is essentially "betting" on "alpha", or excellence as an opportunity for investors.

KSS.name: Kohl's Corporation
KSS.fact: A Polish immigrant named Maxwell Kohl journeyed to Milwaukee, Wisconsin where he established a corner grocery store. As of 2021, Kohl's is the largest department store company in the United States of America.

FWONA.name: Formula One Group
FWONA.fact: Formula One group holds exclusive commercial rights to the FIA Formula One World Championship. Formula 1 racing is considered the world's most prestigious motor racing competition. The race runs for nine months and spans 23 races in 21 countries across five continents.

CMG.name: Chipotle Mexican Grill, Inc.
CMG.fact: Founder Steve Ells started Chipotle in an abandoned ice cream store in 1993.

FFIN.name: First Financial Bankshares, Inc.
FFIN.fact: In 1890, the bank's first year of operation, depositors entrusted the startup from Abilene, Texas with $33,000 - over $1 million in today's money.

TYL.name: Tyler Technologies, Inc.
TYL.fact: Tyler Technologies began offering cloud-based solutions in 2000. Since then, they have amassed over 66,000 users in their Tyler Community. It is estimated that over 5 million people use Tyler technologies in some form including submitting payments and filing court documents.

VIRC.name: Virco Mfg. Corporation
VIRC.fact: This biotech company has pledged to take on some of the world's most infectious diseases, including COVID-19, hepatitis B, influenza A, and HIV.

HTLD.name: Heartland Express, Inc.
HTLD.fact: If you have spent much time driving American highways, you have probably seen a Heartland Express truck. Based in Iowa, Heartland operates a fleet of about 2,400 trucks, making an average hal of 625 miles. Depending on segment, the average driver can earn from  $56,000 to $86,000 annually, with top drivers earning as much as $108,000 a year. The company also may offer free apprenticeships to qualified candidates.

TFX.name: Teleflex Incorporated
TFX.fact: The company began in 1943 with a single product that was used in Spitfire planes in World War II. It was a flexible cable used to adjust the pilot's radio, which was located behind the cockpit and out of the pilot's reach. The flexible cable was used telescopically, to adjust the radio, giving teleflex their name.

JCI.name: Johnson Controls International plc
JCI.fact: Warren Johnson toils for three years to invent a device to regulate room temperature. In 1883, he receives his first patent for what will be known as the electric room thermostat an invention that launches an industry and changes how people live.

MCO.name: Moody's Corporation
MCO.fact: Moody's Corporation traces its history back to two publishing companies established by John Moody, the inventor of modern bond credit ratings.

ESI.name: Element Solutions Inc
ESI.fact: The roots of Element Solutions date back to a metal finishing company that was founded in 1785.

ZTS.name: Zoetis Inc.
ZTS.fact: Spun off from Pfizer, Zoetis is the world leader in medicine and vaccines for animals, including pets and livestock.

CSTE.name: Caesarstone Ltd.
CSTE.fact: In 1987, Caesarstone sparked a revolution in the global countertops market by developing the first quartz surfacing solution - enabling the rise of man-made quartz countertops as a viable alternative to granite.

EPAM.name: EPAM Systems, Inc.
EPAM.fact: EPAM builds custom software and provides consulting via its team of international software engineering talent. It is one of the largest custom software companies for hire in the world, with projects completed for almost every industry imaginable.

COLM.name: Columbia Sportswear Company
COLM.fact: The apparel company has worldwide famous brands that include Columbia, Sorel, Mountain Hard Wear, and Prana.

NJR.name: New Jersey Resources Corporation
NJR.fact: Operates and maintains 7,600 miles of natural gas infrastructure in New Jersey.

POR.name: Portland General Electric Company
POR.fact: This company was founded in 1888 as Falls Electric Company with initial funding from General Electric.

GOOG.name: Alphabet Inc.
GOOG.fact: Google employees in the US get death benefits which guarantee that the surviving spouse will receive 50% of their salary every year for the next decade.

AWI.name: Armstrong World Industries, Inc.
AWI.fact: AWI dates back 155 years to a two-man cork-cutting shop in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. When Thomas Armstrong started selling his product, he put his name on every bag of Armstrong corks with a written guarantee inside the bag because he believed in what he did. His pioneering and American spirit wanted to ensure that "the buyer have faith."

ITW.name: Illinois Tool Works Inc.
ITW.fact: Illinois Tool Works designed equipment that allowed for beverages to be packed in the plastic carriers still used today. This saved beverage companies millions of dollars annually and greatly reduced the environmental impact of excessive packaging.

UNP.name: Union Pacific Corporation
UNP.fact: Union Pacific built 1,085 miles of the legendary transcontinental railroad, spanning from Omaha, Nebraska to Promontory Summit in Utah.

CI.name: Cigna Corporation
CI.fact: Cigna was named to the Dow Jones Sustainability World and North America Indices in 2019 with the leading score for the health care providers and services industry sector.

RCL.name: Royal Caribbean Cruises Ltd.
RCL.fact: Enjoying a show on the cruise ship "Harmony" is more like a night at a Broadway theatre, rather than a cheesy Las Vegas cabaret, with Royal Caribbean securing the rights to "Grease" and casting a talented ensemble to perform the much-loved musical.

CRI.name: Carter's Inc.
CRI.fact: Carter's was established in 1865 by William Carter. The clothing company has since become the largest branded marketer of baby and children's clothing in the U.S., with brands like Carter's and OshKosh B'gosh that serve as two very recognized brands in the nation.

HUN.name: Huntsman Corporation
HUN.fact: Huntsman created a "clamshell" container for the McDonald's Big Mac, which is just one of 80 product inventions.

TROW.name: T. Rowe Price Group, Inc.
TROW.fact: It was founded in 1937 by Thomas Rowe Price, Jr. who was known for developing the growth stock method of investing.

NFLX.name: Netflix, Inc.
NFLX.fact: Netflix streams about six billion hours of material each month!

YELP.name: Yelp Inc.
YELP.fact: Yelp business listings include over 200 million reviews. It logs about 50 million unique visitors each month to its mobile sites and about 40 million via desktop.

BNL.name: Broadstone Net Lease, Inc.
BNL.fact: As of 2022, Broadstone was spread across 43 U.S. States and 4 Canadian Provinces with approximately $5 billion in real estate investments that spread across 752 properties.

FIZZ.name: National Beverage Corp.
FIZZ.fact: National Beverage owns a diverse portfolio of beverages including La Croix, Everfresh, Faygo, Rip It, and more.

SLM.name: SLM Corporation
SLM.fact: Sallie Mae was originally called the Student Loan Marketing Association. It was created for public education loans, but began privatizing its operations in 1997.

ZG.name: Zillow Group, Inc. Class A
ZG.fact: Popular with many people dreaming about their next home, Zillow claims over 250 million monthly visitors, and was founded in 2004 by ex-Microsoft employees.

ORA.name: Ormat Technologies, Inc.
ORA.fact: Ormat understood the importance of innovation. That is why the company developed the Solar Pond Power Plant - an experimental project to develop the use of solar energy production.

ADSK.name: Autodesk, Inc.
ADSK.fact: Autodesk has a group devoted to synthetic biology.

SAIA.name: Saia, Inc.
SAIA.fact: Louis Saia Sr realized that he could make more money delivering produce than he could in selling it - so he used his personal car with the rear seats removed to make the company's first delivery. As of 2020, the trucking company is ranked in the top ten of all LTL carriers in the United States of America.

ROL.name: Rollins, Inc.
ROL.fact: In 1901, Orkin began operations. The child of Latvian immigrants, Otto "The Rat Man" Orkin began selling rat poison door-to-door at the age of 14. He first began developing his own pest control methods at age 12.

BRBR.name: BellRing Brands, Inc.
BRBR.fact: Owner of nutrition brands like PowerBar, Premier Protein, and Dymatize - BellRing's mission is to "Bring Good Energy to the World".

SGRY.name: Surgery Partners, Inc.
SGRY.fact: Owner/Operator of more than 180 locations in 31 states, this company partners with physicians - providing facilties and equipment to enhance their practices.

XPO.name: XPO Logistics, Inc.
XPO.fact: This transportation company has a global network of 731 locations and approximately 42,000 employees.

MLM.name: Martin Marietta Materials, Inc.
MLM.fact: in 2009, Fortune magazine ranked Martin Marietta Materials No. 1 on its "World's Most Admired Company for Building Materials Industry" list.

UIS.name: Unisys Corporation
UIS.fact: Unisys is a global IT and consulting firm.

AME.name: AMETEK, Inc.
AME.fact: Ametek's U.S. Gauge division is the world's largest manufacturer of gauges, while the Microfoam division is the only producer in the world of recyclable polypropylene (plastic) foam sheeting.

CARG.name: CarGurus, Inc.
CARG.fact: Co-founder of TripAdvisor, Langley Steinert, established CarGurus, which quickly became the most visited automotive shopping site in the US.

GDDY.name: GoDaddy Inc.
GDDY.fact: The company "GoDaddy" originally looked into naming the company "Big Daddy," but the domain name was unavailable. Bob Parsons, the Founder, suggested the name GoDaddy, and the company stuck with it.

PVH.name: PVH Corp.
PVH.fact: The company owns three titans of the apparel industry: Calvin Klein, Tommy Hilfiger, and Heritage Brand.

AMAT.name: Applied Materials, Inc.
AMAT.fact: In 1993, the Applied Materials' Precision 5000 was included in the Smithsonian's collection for Information Age Technology.

COUR.name: Coursera, Inc.
COUR.fact: Founded in 2012 by two Stanford University computer science professors, Andrew Ng and Daphne Koller, Coursera partners with more than 200 leading universities to provide online courses.

CTSH.name: Cognizant Technology Solutions Corporation
CTSH.fact: Every hospital patient in the U.S. is asked to complete a Consumer Assessment of Healthcare Providers and Systems (CAHPS) survey. In 2017, a large health network asked Cognizant to analyze its CAHPS data using advanced artificial intelligence and computer science techniques.

FTCI.name: FTC Solar, Inc.
FTCI.fact: FTC Solar helps solar panels capture as much of the sun's energy as possible, by designing and manfufacturing tracking systems to help solar panels continuosly adjust to the optimal angle.

CAT.name: Caterpillar Inc.
CAT.fact: Caterpillar originally painted their equipment gray. They switched to "highway yellow" in 1931.

WING.name: Wingstop Inc.
WING.fact: Wingstop's unique logo derives from the 1930s and 1940s pre-jet aviation themes.

FTV.name: Fortive Corporation
FTV.fact: Fortive is an industrial technology conglomerate that owns over 20 businesses. It was spun off from Danaher in 2016.

BURL.name: Burlington Stores, Inc.
BURL.fact: Burlington began in 1924 as a wholesaler of high quality ladies coats and junior suits - with prices substantially below department store retail prices.

AVO.name: Mission Produce, Inc.
AVO.fact: Do you like avocado toast? Or some game-day guacamole? Mission Produce is the global leader in avocado production. The company owns 3.700 hectares of avocado farms in Peru, where it also operates the world's largest avocado produce packing plant.

WST.name: West Pharmaceutical Services, Inc.
WST.fact: In 2019, West contributed more than 100 scientific publications that furthered the science involved in injectable medicine containment and delivery.

GLPI.name: Gaming and Leisure Properties, Inc.
GLPI.fact: As of 2022, this real estate investment trust (REIT) owns 55 casino properties and leases them out to other companies.

UMBF.name: UMB Financial Corporation
UMBF.fact: UMB traces its roots back more than 100 years, with the Kemper family having a significant influence on the life of the bank. In 1959, the third-generation banker from the Kemper family pioneered the installation of the bank's first computer processing system, representing the ingenuity of the bank for decades to come.

SM.name: SM Energy Company
SM.fact: From its founding in 1908, the SM Energy Company was known as St. Mary Land and Exploration Company until 2010.

SNX.name: TD Synnex Corp
SNX.fact: In 2021, SYNNEX was ranked number 117 on Fortune 200 list, in part, because it distributed more than 40,000 technology products to over 25,000 resellers and retail customers.

CUBE.name: CubeSmart
CUBE.fact: CubeSmart is a REIT that invests in self-storage properties across the United States of America and as of 2019, the company had 36.6 million rentable square feet.

TTEK.name: Tetra Tech, Inc.
TTEK.fact: This tech company launched the first remote control submarine for exploration and military applications.

KO.name: The Coca-Cola Company
KO.fact: Coca-Cola is reportedly the second most widely understood term in the world, after 'ok.'

DLB.name: Dolby Laboratories, Inc.
DLB.fact: Ray Dolby, "The Artist's Inventor", made the sound effects used in Star Wars possible. Thousands of films and billions of products have featured Dolby tech to create higher fidelity and more immersive experiences. In his lifetime, Dolby earned more than 50 US patents.

AMD.name: Advanced Micro Devices, Inc.
AMD.fact: In 1982, Intel and AMD entered into a "technological exchange" agreement. This means that if one company invents a new type of semiconductor, the other company will be next in line to sell it.

NVST.name: Envista Holdings Corp
NVST.fact: Envista is united in a family of more than 30 trusted dental brands.

CPT.name: Camden Property Trust
CPT.fact: Kenneth Schnitzer attended both the universities of Texas and Houston - and dropped out of both. He completed his first real estate deal at the age of 23 and the rest is history. Many credit him with Houston's skyline because of his role in the production of many Houston landmarks such as the Greenway Plaza, the 71-story Wells Fargo Bank Plaza, the 50-story Enron building and more.

ECL.name: Ecolab Inc.
ECL.fact: Ecolab's roots can be traced back to the 1920s, where M.J. Osborn recognized the need for an effective detergent for electric dish machines.

IEX.name: IDEX Corporation
IEX.fact: Idex's subsidiary company created the Jaws of Life. A tool used to save people in car accidents.

NKE.name: NIKE, Inc.
NKE.fact: The Nike swoosh was designed by a Portland State University student for just $35. She was later given stock now worth more than $880,000.

RDVT.name: Red Violet, Inc.
RDVT.fact: RedViolet is engaged in cloud-based data analytics

AOS.name: A. O. Smith Corporation
AOS.fact: In 1899, during the earliest days of the automobile revolution, A. O. Smith developed a new, lightweight steel car frame.

DXC.name: DXC Technology Company
DXC.fact: Electronic Data Systems, a predecessor of DXC, was founded by Ross Perot.

ALLE.name: Allegion plc
ALLE.fact: Allegion invented the "panic release bar" exit device in 1908 and pioneered the first-ever electric-controlled lock.

SJM.name: The J. M. Smucker Company
SJM.fact: Smucker's original apple ciders and butters reportedly used apples from Ohio orchards planted by Johnny Appleseed.

PAYX.name: Paychex, Inc.
PAYX.fact: Paychex pays out 1 of every 12 American private sector employees.

ACN.name: Accenture plc
ACN.fact: Accenture is a common acronym derived from the word accent. The name was suggested by a Danish worker named Kim Peterson.

KREF.name: KKR Real Estate Finance Trust Inc.

DDOG.name: Datadog, Inc.
DDOG.fact: This company's name was originally intended as a codename. However, because Datadog stuck, they decided to make it the official name of the company.

HAYW.name: Hayward Holdings, Inc.
HAYW.fact: The outdoor living company is considered the #1 products brand amongst U.S. pool professionals.

SYY.name: Sysco Corporation
SYY.fact: Sysco estimates that they serve about 16% of the annual $300 billion foodservice market in the U.S. and Canada.

KMPR.name: Kemper Corporation
KMPR.fact: In 2022, Kemper was considered to be one of the U.S.'s leading specialized insurers, with over $15 billion in assets, well over 6 million policies, and approximately 35,000 agents and brokers.

RRBI.name: Red River Bancshares, Inc.
RRBI.fact: Founded in 1999, Red River has averaged better than one new banking location for every year it has been in business.

CNTY.name: Century Casinos, Inc.
CNTY.fact: Headquarted in Colorado Springs, Century Casinos operates 10 casinos in Colorado, West Virginia, Missouri, and Alberta, Canada.

ROP.name: Roper Technologies, Inc.
ROP.fact: Roper Pump Co., a division of Roper, was originally named the Van Wie Gas Stove company. Van Wie paid off all of the company's debts on September 1, 1894 - a fire completely destroyed the facilities just a couple of days later. The plant was rebuilt and renamed Eclipse Gas Stove company.

WWD.name: Woodward, Inc.
WWD.fact: Woodward is very proud of the parts they supplied for the United States of America military's first turbine-powered aircraft.

LSTR.name: Landstar System, Inc.
LSTR.fact: The transportation management solutions company, Landstar, is a Fortune 500 firm.

EOG.name: EOG Resources, Inc.
EOG.fact: In 2015, EOG produced a cumulative 285 million barrels of oil from the Eagle Ford Shale.

STNE.name: StoneCo Ltd.
STNE.fact: When StoneCo was launched in 2012, founders Andre Street and Eduardo Pontes had already spent over a decade working in the electronic payment and payment processing fields in Brazil.

CWEN.name: Clearway Energy, Inc.
CWEN.fact: The renewable energy company possesses more than 4.7 gigawatts of wind, solar, and energy storage assets spread across 25 states as of 2022.

AAPL.name: Apple Inc.
AAPL.fact: Apple scored big time with the iPod. The creator, Tony Fadell, had originally offered the device to both Real Networks and Philips. Both companies turned it down.

AMKR.name: Amkor Technology, Inc.
AMKR.fact: Amkor was recognized as the Supplier of the Year for 2016 by Qualcomm Technologies for the second year in a row.

GME.name: GameStop Corp.
GME.fact:
Perhaps the world's most famous "meme stock", GameStop made headlines across the globe in 2020-2021 as the subject of a fierce battle between hedge funds (who were aggressively "shorting" the stock) and an army of retail investors (who were aggressively buying GME shares).

The resulting stock price volatility even led to congressional hearings featuring a cast of characters as diverse as a Redditor named "Roaring Kitty", the CEO of Robinhood, and the head of the SEC.

PCTY.name: Paylocity Holding Corporation
PCTY.fact: The company's headquarters is the former headquarters of Zurich Insurance North America, located in Schaumburg.

HUBS.name: HubSpot, Inc.
HUBS.fact: HubSpot has achieve impressive growth offering a customer relationship management (CRM platform), supporting the businesses of others with a focus on inbound marketing.

CHH.name: Choice Hotels International, Inc.
CHH.fact: This hotel company owns over 7,000 locations with approximately 570,000 rooms in over 40 countries. Brands include Sleep Inn, Comfort Inn, Cambria and more.

SXT.name: Sensient Technologies Corporation
SXT.fact: Founded in 1882, Sensient was originally a distillery, but due to the prohibition, the company then transformed into the food industry. In 2021, Sensient Technologies was ranked 10th on the Global Top 50 Food Flavors and Fragrances Companies list.

PHM.name: PulteGroup, Inc.
PHM.fact: In 2016, the company was the 3rd largest home construction company in the United States of America, based on the number of homes closed.

AOMR.name: Angel Oak Mortgage, Inc.
AOMR.fact: The Angel Oak is a legendary tree located in South Carolina. It is the largest Live Oak Tree east of the Mississippi, with a trunk circumference of 25.5 feet and 17,000 square feet of shade.

LW.name: Lamb Weston Holdings, Inc.
LW.fact: Lamb Weston is a leading supplier of frozen potato, sweet potato, appetizer and vegetable products to restaurants and retailers around the world.

PRI.name: Primerica, Inc.
PRI.fact: The reason why the founders established Primerica is that many middle-income families were neglected by the financial services industry. So, Primerica decided to make it their mission to teach working families simple money management concepts.

TRV.name: The Travelers Companies, Inc.
TRV.fact: Founded in 1864 in Hartford, Connecticut. Its original purpose was to provide travel insurance to railroad travelers at a time when passenger rail much riskier and dangerous than today.

SIGI.name: Selective Insurance Group, Inc.
SIGI.fact: Many founders derive a business model from unexpected origins. Daniel L.B. Smith adequately fits into that category -  he got into the insurance business because of a runaway horse that wrecked one of his carriages.

CXT.name: Crane NXT, Co.
CXT.fact: On July 4, Crane’s founder R.T. Crane wrote a resolution that would stand as the foundation of the company's culture for more than 150 years.

TK.name: Teekay Corporation
TK.fact: Teekay claims to be the world's largest operator of mid-sized tankers. Its "SuezMax" tankers are classified as such because they are the largest size ship that will still fit through the Suez Canal.

AIG.name: American International Group, Inc.
AIG.fact: The original headquarters of American International Group was located in Shanghai, China.

APPN.name: Appian Corporation
APPN.fact: In 2001, Appian developed Army Knowledge Online, which at the time was regarded as the world's largest intranet.

OLN.name: Olin Corporation
OLN.fact: During both WWI and WWII, Olin played a key role in producing ammunitions and guns. Supporting the war efforts made the Olin's family one of the wealthiest American families of that time.

MSTR.name: Strategy Inc
MSTR.fact: The two co-founders met while students at MIT. In 1992, the BI company landed its first huge client, McDonald's. In the four years following their first client, MicroStrategy increased revenue by 100%.

BKH.name: Black Hills Corporation
BKH.fact: This energy company derives its name from the Black Hills of South Dakota, a mountain range extended in western South Dakota named after its dark appearance.

PFSI.name: PennyMac Financial Services, Inc.
PFSI.fact: As of 2022, PennyMac was the #6 VA Lender and the #7 home loan servicer in the U.S.

CMCSA.name: Comcast Corporation
CMCSA.fact: In 2002, Comcast purchased AT&T Broadband, at the time the largest cable television operator in the U.S., for $44.5 billion.

KMX.name: CarMax, Inc.
KMX.fact: Carmax traditionally gets an influx of trucks and SUV's after gas prices skyrocket.

TEAM.name: Atlassian Corporation
TEAM.fact: One of the more remarkable stories in Australia's tech industry, Atlassian offers software that strives to make project management better and enhance team collaboration. Users totaled over 200,000 at the start of 2022.

OGN.name: Organon & Co.
OGN.fact: Organon is a cutting edge pharmaceutical company focused on science-based medications and treatments for women.

HLNE.name: Hamilton Lane Incorporated
HLNE.fact: With 900+ clients and investors, Hamilton Lane had $901.1 billion in Assets Under Management and Supervision as of 2022.

WAL.name: Western Alliance Bancorporation
WAL.fact: In 2022, the bank was ranked 11th on the Forbes list of America's Best Banks and was ranked as the 51st largest bank in the world.

PCAR.name: PACCAR Inc
PCAR.fact: Paccar is the second largest medium and heavy truck manufacturer in the world.

FNF.name: Fidelity National Financial, Inc.
FNF.fact: The company is ranked favorably on the Fortune 500 list and in 2019, annual revenue nearly reached 8.5 billion dollars.

HLT.name: Hilton Worldwide Holdings Inc.
HLT.fact: Way back in 1971, a young John Lennon was lounging in one of the company's hotels when he decided to do some brainstorming. He ended up writing the word "Imagine" on a piece of the hotel's stationary.

LNG.name: Cheniere Energy, Inc.
LNG.fact: Cheniere specializes in liquified natural gas (LNG) and was the first U.S. company to export LNG. The company has a 25 year agreement to provide LNG to Taiwan, valued at $25 billion through the year 2046

EXPE.name: Expedia Group, Inc.
EXPE.fact: Expedia has sold enough hotel room's in the last 20 years to account for every person currently living in the U.S.

OKTA.name: Okta, Inc.
OKTA.fact: Okta is a cloud software company specializing in identity and access management.

TJX.name: The TJX Companies, Inc.
TJX.fact: Surprisingly, T.J. Maxx is not called T.J. Maxx overseas. Instead, it is named T.K. Maxx to avoid confusion with another popular store called T.J. Hughes.

TXN.name: Texas Instruments Incorporated
TXN.fact: Texas Instruments has a monopoly on the graphing calculator market. They account for about 90% of sales every year.

RTX.name: RTX Corporation
RTX.fact: Raytheon is a large military contractor, earning much of its revenue from the United States of America government. Products engineered include military defense systems, aviation technology, and  even intelligent space technology.

WYNN.name: Wynn Resorts, Limited
WYNN.fact: Wynn actually generates most of its revenue from casinos. Its resorts/room revenue only makes up roughly 12% of total sales.

CDNS.name: Cadence Design Systems, Inc.
CDNS.fact: For six years in a row, Fortune magazine has named Cadence one of the 100 Best Companies to Work For.

UDR.name: UDR, Inc.
UDR.fact: In 2020, this company installed over 831,000 kilowatt hours of solar generation capacity on their properties.

PRGO.name: Perrigo Company plc
PRGO.fact: Founded in 1887 as a packager of home remedies. Perrigo is one of the United States of America' largest manufacturers of nutrition products for the store brand market. Nutrition products include infant formula, pediatric nutritionals and vitamins, minerals, and supplements.

BJ.name: BJ's Wholesale Club Holdings, Inc.
BJ.fact: The company's name is derived from the initials of the daughter of Mervyn Weich (the former president of the company). Her name is Beverly Jean Weich.

CHE.name: Chemed Corporation
CHE.fact: In addition to its core hotel and gaming activities, Red Rock has been occasionally used in television and film for programs such as Hell's Kitchen, Real Housewives of Orange County, and Rock of Love.

CPRI.name: Capri Holdings Limited
CPRI.fact: Capri Holdings Limited was formerly known as Michael Kors Holdings Limited founded by the American designer, Michael Kors. The holding company now owns Versace, Jimmy Choo, and of course, Michael Kors.

CFR.name: Cullen/Frost Bankers, Inc.
CFR.fact: This bank started in the back of a small store in San Antonio in 1868, where Frost provided frontiersmen the essential supplies they needed to survive.

BHB.name: Bar Harbor Bankshares
BHB.fact: Founded in 1887, Bar Harbor Bank operates over 50 locations across Maine, New Hampshire, and Vermont. Assets totalled nearly $4 billion, as of late 2021.

GMED.name: Globus Medical, Inc.
GMED.fact: Globus helps people with musculosketal problems by manufacturing artificial joints and orthopedic implants.

NLY.name: Annaly Capital Management, Inc.
NLY.fact: One of the largest mortgage REIT's in the U.S., Annaly has over $11 billion in permanent capital.

MA.name: Mastercard Incorporated
MA.fact: By using Mastercard's payroll system, Walmart saves over 250,000 lbs of paper checks each year

LYFT.name: Lyft, Inc.
LYFT.fact: The co-founder of Lyft, Logan Green, received inspiration for the idea after sharing rides from the University of California - Santa Barbara to Los Angeles to visit his girlfriend. The company was known for its pink mustaches as a way of identifying Lyft drivers. Upon meeting, the riders were encouraged to sit in the front seat and fist bump the driver - they have since stepped away from that means of introduction.

STAA.name: STAAR Surgical Company
STAA.fact: Since the founding of the company in 1991, STAAR has sold over 2,000,000 lenses.

LZ.name: LegalZoom.com, Inc.
LZ.fact: LegalZoom has helped 2+ million entrepreneurs turn ideas into businesses and over 650,000 consultations to a network of attorneys. Robert Shapiro, famed attorney from the OJ Simpson trial, was one of the founders.

LYV.name: Live Nation Entertainment, Inc.
LYV.fact: Live Nation owns Front Line Management, the world's top artist management company, which reps over 250 major artists. It is also the parent company of Ticketmaster.

MDT.name: Medtronic Plc
MDT.fact: In 2008, a team of computer security researchers was able to take remote control of a Medtronic cardiac implant. The team, using an unused implant in a lab, was able to control the electrical shocks delivered by the defibrillator component and even glean patient data from the device

HXL.name: Hexcel Corporation
HXL.fact: Founded in the basement of Roger Steel's suburban home after Steel and co-founder Roscoe Hughes returned home from the Navy post-WWII. Their innovations and hard work would not stop in that basement. In fact,  Hexcel went on to produce the lunar struts of the Apollo 11 lunar landing module.

RSI.name: Rush Street Interactive, Inc.
RSI.fact: Rush Street Interactive, Inc. operates as an online casino and sports betting company in the United States of America and Latin America. It provides real-money online casino, online and retail sports wagering, and social gaming services.

BL.name: BlackLine, Inc.
BL.fact: BlackLine was created to provide unified cloud solutions for the finance and accounting industries.

PLNT.name: Planet Fitness, Inc.
PLNT.fact: Known as the "judgment free zone," Planet Fitness created what they call the "lunk alarm." This alarm is designed to prevent unwanted behavior by the users.

ODFL.name: Old Dominion Freight Line, Inc.
ODFL.fact: In 1934, Earl and Lillian Congdon founded Old Dominion Freight Line with a single truck running from Richmond, VA and Norfolk, VA. Today, Old Dominion Freight Line is a global transportation company with 20,000 employees.

PD.name: PagerDuty, Inc.
PD.fact: PagerDuty employees are called "Dutonians". Focused on a "duty" to giving back, the company is part of the "1% Pledge" meaning that PagerDuty has promised to give 1% of its Equity, Time, Product, and Profit to philanthropic efforts.

IBP.name: Installed Building Products, Inc.
IBP.fact: From its humble beginnings as a small insulation company in Columbus, Ohio, Installed Building Products has grown to become one of the largest insulation installers in the residential new construction market in the U.S.

GEHC.name: GE HealthCare Technologies Inc.
GEHC.fact: Spun-off from General Electric in 2022, GE HealthCare is a world leader in medical equipment manufacturing, with over 50,000 employees across the globe.

KTOS.name: Kratos Defense & Security Solutions, Inc.
KTOS.fact: Sharing a name with protagonist of the video game series, "God of War", Kratos leadership has deep experience working with the U.S. Dept of Defense, Dept of Homeland Security, and various branches of the military. The company is involved in drone, missile defense, electronic warfare, space systems, communications, and training systems.

PFGC.name: Performance Food Group Co
PFGC.fact: This company's roots go back to 1885, when James Capers began peddling groceries for a wholesaler in Richmond, Va.

MKTX.name: MarketAxess Holdings Inc.
MKTX.fact: MarketAxess provides electronic trading systems for 84% of high-yield debt traders.

MUR.name: Murphy Oil Corporation
MUR.fact: In 1953, Charlie Murphy Sr. backed the development of a submersible drilling barge that took offshore rigs into deep waters. This development was fundamental for deepwater offshore drilling - so they named the prototype the "Mr. Charlie."

DK.name: Delek US Holdings, Inc.
DK.fact: Having nothing to do with "Dr. Who", Delek refines over 300,000 barrels of crude oil each day at its four refineries.

BPOPM.name: Popular Capital Trust II PFD GTD 6.125%
BPOPM.fact: This Puerto Rico-based bank that began operations in 1893, establishing itself when Puerto Rico was still under Spanish administration.

TTC.name: The Toro Company
TTC.fact: The Toro company invented the first mechanized fairway mower in 1919. IN 1942, the American company ceased production of domestic products to support the U.S. war effort.

EVR.name: Evercore Inc.
EVR.fact: Since its founding, Evercore has advised over $4.7 trillion in merger, acquisition, and restructuring transactions.

CMS.name: CMS Energy Corporation
CMS.fact: Consumers Energy owns over 71,000 miles of electrical distribution lines.

BMY.name: Bristol-Myers Squibb Company
BMY.fact: In 1998 the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) granted the company permission to market Excedrin Migraine, the first migraine headache pain medication available to consumers without a prescription.

JKHY.name: Jack Henry & Associates, Inc.
JKHY.fact: Jack Henry and Jerry Hall were believed to have been the only two computer users in Monett, Missouri - a small town in the picturesque lake region of the Ozark Mountains.

WY.name: Weyerhaeuser Company
WY.fact: Weyerhaeuser Co. is one of the world's largest private owners of timberlands, owning or controlling nearly 12.4 million acres of timberlands across the U.S. and managing an additional 14 million acres under long-term licenses in Canada.

ATOM.name: Atomera Incorporated
ATOM.fact: Atomera's patented quantum-engineered material, named Mears Silicon Technology (MST), significantly extends mobile phone battery life and enables manufacture of smaller IoT devices.

VFC.name: V.F. Corporation
VFC.fact: VF owns 55% of the US backpack market. Its major brands include Jansport, Eastpak, Timberland, and North Face.

MGM.name: MGM Resorts International
MGM.fact: MGM features a 100,000 lb bronze lion statue at the corner of Las Vegas Blvd and Tropicana Ave. It is 45 feet tall and is perched on top of a 25 foot statue. It is the largest bronze statue in the U.S.

PEG.name: Public Service Enterprise Group Incorporated
PEG.fact: PSEG named one of Americas Most JUST Companies for 2020, according to Forbes and JUST Capital, recognizing New Jerseys largest energy provider as a national leader in categories such as ethical leadership, equal opportunity, customer treatment, community support and environmental impact.

AFL.name: Aflac Incorporated
AFL.fact: In 2000, the Aflac Duck campaign debuted with the television commercial "Park Bench." Though founded in the United States of America, Aflac has had incredible success in Japan, insuring one out of every four Japanese households.

BRO.name: Brown & Brown, Inc.
BRO.fact: J. Hyatt Brown, son of the co-founder Adrian Brown, became CEO in 1961 and grew the family-owned insurance agency from a single office in Daytona Beach, Florida, into one of the nation's largest insurance brokerages. During his role as CEO, J. Hyatt Brown also served as a member of the Florida House of Representatives.

VITL.name: Vital Farms, Inc.
VITL.fact: Enjoy eggs? Vital Farms is obsessed with them. Every Vital Farms organic egg comes for a pasture-raised hen.

DKS.name: DICK'S Sporting Goods, Inc.
DKS.fact: Dick's is America's largest sporting goods retailer, with over 800 stores and approximately 50,000 employees. The company was founded in 1948 by 18 year-old Richard "Dick" Stack, who was able to turn his love of sports into a business, thanks to a $300 loan from his grandmother.

CHGG.name: Chegg, Inc.
CHGG.fact: Why is this company called Chegg? The name is a combination of "Chicken" and "Egg". Chegg was founded in 2000 by three friends from Iowa State University, who decided to solve a problem. How do you get a job without experience? How do you get experience without a job? Today, the company offers book rentals and sales, homework assistance, and other student services.

SMCI.name: Super Micro Computer, Inc.
SMCI.fact: SMCI's manufacturing facility in San Jose was designed to meet LEED gold certification. The company also has locations in the Netherlands and Taiwan.

BKNG.name: Booking Holdings Inc.
