BKNG.fact: Booking owns 6 popular traveling brands. Their brands are Booking.com, priceline, KAYAK, agoda.com, Rentalcars.com, and OpenTable.

SIG.name: Signet Jewelers Limited
SIG.fact: Signet Jewelers is the owner of major jewelry brands Zales, Kay Jewelers, Jared, Banter, James Allen, Ernest Jones, H. Samuel, rocksbox, and Peoples - "Canada's #1 Diamond Store".

WK.name: Workiva Inc.
WK.fact: Workiva was ranked in Fortune 100 Best places to Work for three years in a row.

IVZ.name: Invesco Ltd.
IVZ.fact: Invesco subscribes to research from two of the world's leading proxy advisory firms, Glass Lewis and International Shareholder Services.

DRVN.name: Driven Brands Holdings Inc.
DRVN.fact: Driven Brands is the parent company of some of leading automotive business services such as Take 5 Oil Change, Meineke Car Care Centers, Maaco, and more.

MCHP.name: Microchip Technology Incorporated
MCHP.fact: Held in locations around the world, Microchips MASTERs Conferences are the premier technical training conferences for embedded control engineers.

OMC.name: Omnicom Group Inc.
OMC.fact: Omniwomen, a global organization within Omnicom, is dedicated to promoting networking and career opportunities, as well as developing the female leaders of tomorrow.

HPP.name: Hudson Pacific Properties, Inc.
HPP.fact: In 2006, Victor Coleman founded Hudson Capital (later renamed Hudson Pacific) using funds from the sale of his prior company, Arden Realty. With its millions of square feet of office buildings and sound stages, the real estate company has since grown to be the largest independent operator of sound stages in Los Angeles.

CHRW.name: C.H. Robinson Worldwide, Inc.
CHRW.fact: Anheuser-Busch InBev is the largest producer of beer in the world. They were looking for a better system to conduct daily spot bids. C.H. Robinson created an AI-assisted pricing tool, a direct digital connection between C.H. Robinson and Anheuser-Busch, that prices and accepts thousands of shipments in less than a few seconds without human interaction.

AWK.name: American Water Works Company, Inc.
AWK.fact: The company was founded in 1886 as American Water Works & Guarantee in Pennsylvania and is listed today on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker symbol AWK. They are the only water utility member of the Dow Jones Utility Average.

ANET.name: Arista Networks, Inc.
ANET.fact: Arista builds scalable data centers for many Fortune 500 companies and delivers products worldwide through distribution partners, systems integrators, and resellers with a strong dedication to partner and customer success.

AMG.name: Affiliated Managers Group, Inc.
AMG.fact: As of 2022, AMG had $814 billion in assets under management.

OMCL.name: Omnicell, Inc.
OMCL.fact: The healthcare technology services company was founded by Randall Lipps after his daughter was hospitalized and the nurses did not know where things were. This prompted in him the idea and vision to develop the industry.

BDX.name: Becton, Dickinson and Company
BDX.fact: BD was one of the first companies to sell U.S.-made glass syringes.

CDW.name: CDW Corporation
CDW.fact: CDW works with 85% of hospital organizations in the United States of America.

MU.name: Micron Technology, Inc.
MU.fact: McDonald's (yes, the one with Ronald McDonald) was one of the earliest investors in this dynamic tech company.

ES.name: Eversource Energy
ES.fact: Eversource Energy provides service to more than 4.3 million electricity, natural gas, and water customers.

BLDR.name: Builders FirstSource, Inc.
BLDR.fact: In 2020, the Fortune 500 company had just shy of $20 billion in sales with over 25,000 employees and over 500 locations.

WIX.name: Wix.com Ltd.
WIX.fact: Within three years of the Israeli-based company's founding, one million people had used Wix's services.

WEC.name: WEC Energy Group, Inc.
WEC.fact: WEC already achieves about 25 percent of its energy from carbon-free generation, including ownership of the two largest wind generation sites in Wisconsin.

NEM.name: Newmont Corporation
NEM.fact: Newmont is currently the world's largest corporate producer of gold, with over 5.8 million ounces mined in calendar year 2020. With operations in North America, South America, Africa, and Australia, the company also produces copper, silver, zinc, and lead. Canada-based Barrick Gold is a top competitor.

ABT.name: Abbott Laboratories
ABT.fact: Abbott's new flash glucose monitoring technology eliminates the need for routine finger pricks.

LLY.name: Eli Lilly and Company
LLY.fact: Lilly's most notable achievements include being the first company to mass-produce the polio vaccine.

EME.name: EMCOR Group, Inc.
EME.fact: Emcor is ranked on the Fortune 500 list with approximately 33,000 employees.

BEN.name: Franklin Resources, Inc.
BEN.fact: The company was founded in 1947 in New York by Rupert H. Johnson, Sr., who ran a successful retail brokerage firm from an office on Wall Street. He named the company after US founding father Benjamin Franklin because Franklin epitomized the ideas of frugality and prudence when it came to saving and investing. The company's first line of mutual funds, Franklin Custodian Funds, was a series of conservatively managed equity and bond funds designed to appeal to most investors.

BAH.name: Booz Allen Hamilton Holding Corporation
BAH.fact: Edwin Booz established the company at the beginning of World War I, in 1914, intending to provide a human touch to management. His business gave birth to the modern management consulting profession with the focus on "people, not products."

PTON.name: Peloton Interactive, Inc.
PTON.fact: Founded in 2012, Peloton's stationary bikes and video classes took America by storm, in addition to providing some popular memes. Peloton users bike through over 130 million workouts each quarter, with over 2 million bikes sold since inception.

LMND.name: Lemonade, Inc.
LMND.fact: Lemonade employees are called "makers". The company started in 2015 with a focus on providing renter's insurance, but has since expanded to also cover homes and pets, with additional plans in the works to insure cars.

CCI.name: Crown Castle Inc.
CCI.fact: Crown Castle has a network of over 40,000 cell towers across the country.

BKE.name: The Buckle, Inc.
BKE.fact: Started in Kearney, Nebraska back in 1948, The Buckle was originally famous for selling rugged, high quality denim to men.  Today, the company now does equally robust business with women and owns numerous other brands, including Hurley, Billabong, Oakley, and more. Its revolutionary e-commerce store enables shoppers in over 200 countries to view and order products in their own local currency.

SGHT.name: Sight Sciences, Inc.
SGHT.fact: Sight Sciences offers the OMNI Surgical System, a device used by ophthalmic surgeons to treat glaucoma patients. It also produces the TearCare System, a wearable system to treat dry eye disease (DED).

EXPD.name: Expeditors International of Washington, Inc.
EXPD.fact: Specialists in logistics and freight forwarding, Expeditors plays an important role in "just-in-time" supply chains.

PB.name: Prosperity Bancshares, Inc.
PB.fact: As of March 2022, the bank operates in 272 full-service banking locations.

SSTI.name: SoundThinking, Inc.
SSTI.fact: ShotSpotter's gunshot detection system can identify if a gunshot was fired in a neighborhood, then notify law enforcement to dispatch police response.

RARE.name: Ultragenyx Pharmaceutical Inc.
RARE.fact: This pharmaceutical company owns brand names such as Mepsevii, Crysvita, Dojolvi, and Evkeeza.

JBHT.name: J.B. Hunt Transport Services, Inc.
JBHT.fact: J.B. Hunt Transport Services began as a small carrier of rice hulls from eastern Arkansas.

DOCU.name: DocuSign, Inc.
DOCU.fact: When a customer uses DocuSign, their signatures and documents are uploaded, encrypted, and a unique hash is created. It is estimated that over 20 billion pieces of paper have been saved as a result of the technology.

D.name: Dominion Energy, Inc.
D.fact: Dominion Energy partnered with the Department of Veterans Services and committed to providing energy efficiency improvements to at least 100 homes for 100 veterans who live in Virginia.

AVT.name: Avnet, Inc.
AVT.fact: Avnet is named after the founder, Charles Avnet. Its history began in 1921 on the famous Radio Rows of U.S. cities. During WWII, Avnet made antennas for the U.S. armed forces.

WEN.name: The Wendy's Company
WEN.fact: The name "Wendy's" derives itself from founder Dave Thomas's daughter's nickname - Wendy. The old-fashioned hamburger joint quickly became known for its square hamburgers that hung over the bun and have since continued to share the founder's legacy by naming several items from the menu after Dave.

DLTR.name: Dollar Tree, Inc.
DLTR.fact: In 1986, a predecessor company of Dollar Tree was started. The Only One Dollar store was started by Macon Brock, Doug Perry, and Ray Compton.

SAM.name: The Boston Beer Company, Inc.
SAM.fact: The Boston Beer Company owns Samuel Adams, Dogfish Head, Truly, Twisted Tea, Angry Orchard, and more.

DTE.name: DTE Energy Company
DTE.fact: In June of 1851, 53 gas street lamps were erected on Woodward, Woodbridge, and Jefferson Avenues to light Detroit for the first time. Detroit Gas Light, a predecessor of DTE, powered these lights.

TRC.name: Tejon Ranch Co.
TRC.fact: Established in 1843 by a Mexican land grant, Tejon Ranch is the largest private landholding in California. Kit Carson and Jedediah Smith are just two of the famous pioneers who spent time exploring this vast frontier.

AFG.name: American Financial Group, Inc.
AFG.fact: In 2004, American Financial Group was ranked 488th on the Fortune 500 list.

HPE.name: Hewlett Packard Enterprise Company
HPE.fact: The one-car garage behind 367 Addison Avenue in Palo Alto, California doubled as a workshop for co-founders Bill Hewlett and Dave Packard. It was in this garage where they innovated and manufactured what would become the company's first product, the 200A Audio Oscillator. The garage holds such historic value that the location is recognized as the Birthplace of Silicon Valley".

TDC.name: Teradata Corporation
TDC.fact: A collaboration between researchers at Citibank and Caltech produced Teradata.

WSM.name: Williams-Sonoma, Inc.
WSM.fact: In addition to its namesake kitchen and furnishing stores, Williams Sonoma is also the parent company of Pottery Barn, West Elm, Rejuvenation, and Mark and Graham.

SCHL.name: Scholastic Corporation
SCHL.fact: Scholastic owns the U.S. publishing rights to Harry Potter and is the world's largest publisher and distributor of children's books. Founded in Pittsburgh in 1920, the company is now based in New York City.

CBRL.name: Cracker Barrel Old Country Store
CBRL.fact: Cracker Barrel has been making its own cornbread, fresh and from scratch, for over 50 years.

RRX.name: Regal Rexnord Corporation
RRX.fact: Regal Beloit has humble beginnings and initially started operations in a converted roller rink. That did not stop innovation and expansion for this company. More than sixty years after the founding of Regal Rexnord, the firm was ranked 763rd on the Fortune 1000, with over 28,000 employees in 2021.

MTD.name: Mettler-Toledo International Inc.
MTD.fact: Mettler-Toledo is all about precision measurement. Its XPE Analytical Balances are equipped with the unique StaticDetect technology which automatically detects electrostatically charged samples as soon as these are placed on the weighing pan.

WERN.name: Werner Enterprises, Inc.
WERN.fact: Founded in 1956, Werner is one of the largest trucking companies in the United States of America, with roughly 8,000 trucks and nearly 25,000 trailers.

JLL.name: Jones Lang LaSalle Incorporated
JLL.fact: JLL has offices in 80 countries and nearly 100,000 employees. The firm is considered one of the "Big Three" commercial real estate services companies in the world.

VTRS.name: Viatris Inc.
VTRS.fact: Viatris has the capacity to manufacture 80+ billion doses.

SCI.name: Service Corporation International
SCI.fact: Service Corporation International, as of 2022, had 1,900 locations positioned in 44 states, eight Canadian Provinces, and the District of Columbia.

AGCO.name: AGCO Corporation
AGCO.fact: AGCO has acquired several of the most popular agricultural machinery brands such as Challenger, Fendt, Massey Ferguson, Valtra, and more.

XRX.name: Xerox Holdings Corporation
XRX.fact: Xerographic reproduction was effectively illegal in the Soviet Union until its collapse.

FHI.name: Federated Hermes, Inc.
FHI.fact: Federated Investors was founded in 1955 by three classmates from Pittsburgh's famed Central Catholic High School - John F. Donahue, Richard B. Fisher, and Thomas J. Donnelly. In 2018, the firm acquired a 60% stake in Hermes Fund Managers, with a rebranding completed in 2020 to the current name.

GS.name: The Goldman Sachs Group, Inc.
GS.fact: Goldman Sachs has one of the highest Revenue per Employee figures in the world, approx. $1.41 million per employee annually, as of 2Q 2021.

RLI.name: RLI Corp.
RLI.fact: RLI initially emerged as one of the first insurers of contact lenses and has since developed into additional forms of insurance.

W.name: Wayfair Inc.
W.fact: Wayfair is an e-commerce platform offering more than 15 million items for sale, from more than 23,000 global suppliers.

TFSL.name: TFS Financial Corporation
TFSL.fact: During the Depression in the 1930s, Ben Stefanski and his wife applied for a federal charter to create a savings and loan association to keep the dream of home ownership alive for millions of Ohio residents who were unemployed. The couple was so eager to get this idea started that they applied for the charter on their honeymoon.

SEDG.name: SolarEdge Technologies, Inc.
SEDG.fact: In 2015, SolarEdge partnered with the juggernaut known as Tesla Motors to develop photovoltaic storage and backup power solutions for the residential solar market.

OLLI.name: Ollie's Bargain Outlet Holdings, Inc.
OLLI.fact: In 1990, Ollie's started the unique loyalty program, "Ollie's Army," began, which rewarded loyal shoppers.

AAL.name: American Airlines Group Inc.
AAL.fact: In 1973, American Airlines hired the first female pilot for a commercial airline. Her name is Bonnie Tiburzi who, at 24 years old, started her job with American. She stayed with the company for 26 years. She was the first woman in the world to earn a Flight Engineer rating on a turbo-jet aircraft.

TKR.name: The Timken Company
TKR.fact: Timken specializes in propulsion drivetrain and power transmission systems for naval vessels. The firm is a key contributor to the United States of America Navy's new USS Congress class of frigates.

LVS.name: Las Vegas Sands Corp.
LVS.fact: Las Vegas Sands own their own fleet of aircraft, including eight full size Boeing and Airbus planes along with ten smaller private jets. This fleet is used to transport its executive officers and VIP to its main properties in Las Vegas, Macau, and Singapore.

ARW.name: Arrow Electronics, Inc.
ARW.fact: The electronics company was established by Maurice Goldberg in the "birthplace of electronics" in the heart of lower Manhattan selling used radios and radio parts.

OKE.name: ONEOK, Inc.
OKE.fact: ONEOKs operations include a 38,000-mile integrated network of NGL and natural gas pipelines, processing plants, fractionators and storage facilities in the Mid-Continent, Williston, Permian and Rocky Mountain regions.

INSM.name: Insmed Incorporated
INSM.fact: Non-cancerous lung diseases are the target of Insmed.

MSFT.name: Microsoft Corporation
MSFT.fact: Microsoft is one of the largest corporate collectors of artworks with over 5,000 contemporary pieces including painting, sculpture, works on paper, photographs, ceramics, studio glass, and multimedia works.

LHX.name: L3Harris Technologies, Inc.
LHX.fact: L3Harris has provided navigation technology for every U.S. GPS satellite ever launched. Nearly 3.3 million U.S. jobs rely heavily on GPS tech.

UGI.name: UGI Corporation
UGI.fact: In 2021, the company committed itself to investing over $1 billion in renewable energy solutions over the next 5 years.

STE.name: STERIS plc
STE.fact: Steris is on the front lines of battling COVID-19. Its V-PRO machines are used in hospitals to decontaminate N95 surgical respirators, protecting thousands of healthcare workers.

FSLR.name: First Solar, Inc.
FSLR.fact: In 2011, First Solar ranked first on Forbes's list of America's 25 fastest-growing technology companies and was ranked number 1 in Solar Power World magazine's 2012 and 2013 ranking.

XRAY.name: DENTSPLY SIRONA Inc.
XRAY.fact: Dentsply Sirona is an American dental equipment maker and dental consumables producer that markets its products in over 120 countries. It has factories in 21 countries.

HIG.name: The Hartford Insurance Group, Inc.
HIG.fact: This company has shared life-saving fire safety skills with 110 million kids across the U.S. - Stop, Drop, and Roll!

ASH.name: Ashland Inc.
ASH.fact: Ashland was founded in 1924, by three Swiss Oil executives, with an initial capital investment of $250,000.

AEO.name: American Eagle Outfitters, Inc.
AEO.fact: American Eagle Outfitters gives back through the AEO Foundation, which supports a homeless children's education fund, foster programs, food banks, and environmental conservation efforts.

LMT.name: Lockheed Martin Corporation
LMT.fact: The commercial airplane Lockheed Martin is working on is intended to be the world's first supersonic business jet, flying at three times the speed of sound. At that speed, a plane could cross the country in about 90 minutes, four times faster than the current 5-6 hour flight time.

ZBH.name: Zimmer Biomet Holdings, Inc.
ZBH.fact: Before the merger with Biomet, Zimmer offered more than 130,000 orthopedic products for treating hips, knees, shoulders, elbows, foot and ankle and spine conditions.

CCK.name: Crown Holdings, Inc.
CCK.fact: Founded in the 1890's, Crown once specialized in cork and cork-sealed containers. Today, the company is a global leader in metal containers and specialty packaging.

AYI.name: Acuity Brands, Inc.
AYI.fact: After serving in WWI, Isadore Weinstein founded a linen company. The company was so successful that it was accused of violating anti-trust laws. Subsequently, the company diversified and has evolved into industrial lighting. Acuity is now the largest lighting manufacturer in North America.

EBC.name: Eastern Bankshares, Inc.
EBC.fact: Founded in 1818, Eastern Bankshares has evolved from a modest savings bank to a full-service commercial bank. More than 200 years later, the bank has approximately $24 billion in assets under management as of 2022.

MAS.name: Masco Corporation
MAS.fact: The company's first contract came in 1930 with the Hudson Motor Company valued at $7,000.00

ABNB.name: Airbnb, Inc.
ABNB.fact: Founded in 2008, Airbnb offers more than 6 million places to stay, with locations around the world. For those who demand seclusion, homes are even available in Mongolia, Greenland, and St. Helena (where Napoleon died).

CPA.name: Copa Holdings, S.A.
CPA.fact: Copa Holdings is Panama's leader in airline passenger and cargo services.

DBX.name: Dropbox, Inc.
DBX.fact: The Founder of Dropbox, Drew Houston, came up with the idea after consistently forgetting his USB flash drive while attending MIT.

MAC.name: The Macerich Company
MAC.fact: The name of the real estate company is a portmanteau of the founders, Mace Seige and Richard Cohen.

PLTK.name: Playtika Holding Corp.
PLTK.fact: in 2021, Playtika had roughly 35 million monthly active users playing a wide variety of casino games including Bingo Blitz, World Series of Poker, Solitaire Grand Harvest, and more.

SPCE.name: Virgin Galactic Holdings, Inc.
SPCE.fact: Virgin Galactic blasted its founder, Sir Richard Branson, into space on July 11, 2021. Though he once declined being dropped 354 ft over Africa's Victoria Falls in a specially designed container, Branson had no qualms about being launched 53.5 miles above the earth's crust to become both the first billionaire and knight to reach the requisite altitude. His rival, Amazon founder Jeff Bezos, would follow just nine days later in a spacecraft developed by his own company, Blue Origin.

CPRT.name: Copart, Inc.
CPRT.fact: Copart experiences over 1 million vehicle searches per day and sells a vehicle every 7 seconds.

AVY.name: Avery Dennison Corporation
AVY.fact: Ray Stanton (Stan) Avery invented the worlds first self-adhesive label as a way to merchandise objects. In 1935, he founded Avery Adhesives in downtown Los Angeles and, in 1990, the company merged with Dennison Manufacturing to form Avery Dennison.

KWR.name: Quaker Houghton
KWR.fact: With over 4k employees serving more than 110 countries, Quaker claims to be the global leader in industrial process fluids.

FELE.name: Franklin Electric Co., Inc.
FELE.fact: Franklin Electric was named after one of America's Founding Fathers and pioneers of electrical engineering, Benjamin Franklin.

DGICA.name: Donegal Group Inc.
DGICA.fact: Donegal Insurance specializes in property and casualty. The company has achieved an A.M. Best Rating of A (Excellent) for financial strength relative to coverage.

FHN.name: First Horizon Corporation
FHN.fact: Founded during the American Civil War in 1864. In 1914, the bank helped in organizing the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis. First Horizon is now the largest bank in Tennessee.

MTSI.name: MACOM Technology Solutions Holdings, Inc.
MTSI.fact: The tech company was founded in the 1950s and was a small supplier of magnetrons to the U.S. Army Signal Corps. MACOM is now a producer of radio, microwave, and millimeter wave semiconductor devices.

BLNK.name: Blink Charging Co.
BLNK.fact: Blink Charging is involved in building out capacity to charge electric vehicles. The company offers both residential and commercial equipment, across the U.S. and Canada, as well as its own cloud network supporting EV analytics and management. As of January 2022, charging fees ranged from $0.39 to $0.79 per kWh.

NYT.name: The New York Times Company
NYT.fact: A series of New York Times articles aided in bringing down the corrupt Tweed Ring and its domination over City Hall after William "Boss" Tweed was convicted of stealing millions of dollars of NYC taxpayer money.

BSX.name: Boston Scientific Corporation
BSX.fact: A new study may help better understand how the COVID-19 virus affects people with heart conditions or chronic illnesses and improves their health care. In collaboration with Boston Scientific, a research team from Yale New Haven Hospitals Center for Outcomes Research & Evaluation (CORE) hopes to accomplish this by studying data from pacemakers and defibrillators remotely monitored by the LATITUDE Home Monitoring System in patients with COVID-19. The Boston Scientific devices in the study offer some of the most advanced heart rhythm management technologies available.

EPR.name: EPR Properties
EPR.fact: Founded in 1923, by Joseph Bruening in Cleveland, Ohio. Since its infancy, the company has grown to a global presence in more than 560 operating facilities.

EIX.name: Edison International
EIX.fact: Edison International traces its origins back to July 4, 1886. On that day, predecessor Holt and Knupp first used a steam engine that was fueled by cordwood to power arc lights during Visalia, California's 4th of July celebrations.

MRVL.name: Marvell Technology, Inc.
MRVL.fact: With over 10,000 patents worldwide, it is no wonder why Marvell Technology is trusted by many leading technology companies.

PLCE.name: The Children's Place, Inc.
PLCE.fact: A well-known retailer of clothing for children and infants, The Children's Place is also the parent company of Gymboree, which it acquired out of bankruptcy in 2019.

ILMN.name: Illumina, Inc.
ILMN.fact: In late 2015, Illumina spun off the company Grail, focused on blood testing for cancer tumors in the bloodstream. The company has plans in 2017 to raise $1 billion in its second round of financing, and has received funding from Bill Gates and Jeff Bezos who invested over $100 million in Series A funding, with Illumina maintaining a 20% holding share in Grail.

CWK.name: Cushman & Wakefield plc
CWK.fact: Founded in 1917, Cushman & Wakefield has long been a part of the real estate industry. They have well over 50,000 employees serving across 60 countries.

JBLU.name: JetBlue Airways Corporation
JBLU.fact: The founders of this New York-based company initially wanted to call the airline "Taxi" and to have a yellow livery to associate with New York. However, that idea was shot down by investors, so the founders settled on "NewAir," which was later changed to Jet Blue Airways.

ROG.name: Rogers Corporation
ROG.fact: With over 180 years of experience, Rogers Corporation is one of the oldest publically traded companies in the U.S. The firm was established by Peter Rogers and was initially a paper manufacturer. In 1852, his son, Henry Rogers, invented a process to remove dye from paper, which revolutionized the paper industry.

PNC.name: The PNC Financial Services Group, Inc.
PNC.fact: PNC Tower ranks among the "greenest" skyscrapers ever built, exceeding criteria for LEED Platinum certification. The building's solar chimney, solar collector, and other innovative systems enable a net-zero energy state for much of the year.

APPS.name: Digital Turbine, Inc.
APPS.fact: Digital Turbine is an advertising agency company that claims a 1.5 billion monthly reach.

HALO.name: Halozyme Therapeutics, Inc.
HALO.fact: Halozyme has a state-of-the-art drug delivery system that it calls "ENHANZE," which is based on its proprietary enzyme rHuPH20.

NCNO.name: nCino, Inc.
NCNO.fact: As of 2022, the banking software company services more than 1,500 financial institutions ranging in assets from $30 million to $2 trillion.

NNI.name: Nelnet, Inc.
NNI.fact: Nelnet specializes in administration and repayment of student loans, as well as educational financial services. Following a 2018 acquisition of Great Lakes Educational Loan Services, Inc., Nelnet became the largest servicer of student loans in the U.S., with approximately $400 billion in loans.

PNR.name: Pentair plc
PNR.fact: Through Project Safewater, the company's holistic approach to providing safe water solutions, Pentair collaborates with a range of partners on innovative approaches combining technology, micro-enterprise business models, and scientific research to provide sustainable access to safe water.

RYAM.name: Rayonier Advanced Materials Inc.
RYAM.fact: Rayonier Advanced Materials is a pioneer in manufacturing the highest quality wood-based acetate-grade cellulose - so high-quality, in fact, that it is used in creation of LCD touch screens. In addition, the company manufactures high-value ethers used to develop slow-release medications, specialty cellulose for advanced automotive filters, hot dog and sausage casings, and even fluff pulp used in super absorbent diapers.

SPG.name: Simon Property Group, Inc.
SPG.fact: Co-founder, Melvin Simon, was the son of immigrants. He majored in accounting, served in the U.S. Army, and sold encyclopedias door-to-door, before learning the real estate business as a leasing agent.

APO.name: Apollo Global Management, Inc.
APO.fact: Apollo Global Management ranks among the world's top-tier private equity firms, with over $500 billion in assets under management. Some notable past transactions include acquiring 90% of Yahoo, ADT, Shutterfly, Michaels, and Chuck E. Cheese.

XMTR.name: Xometry, Inc.
XMTR.fact: No manufacturer wants to spend a fortune on tooling for mass production, when prototypes can be created and vetted first. Xometry meets this need with on-demand prototyping.

STX.name: Seagate Technology Holdings plc
STX.fact: Seagate created the first 5.25 inch hard disk drive (HDD).

CAH.name: Cardinal Health, Inc.
CAH.fact: Cardinal Health serves nearly 90% of US hospitals.

TEX.name: Terex Corporation
TEX.fact: Do you like giant cranes and other large machines? Terex does. The company manufactures aerial work platforms and materials processing machinery for customers on six continents. Its Terex Demag CC 8800-1 TWIN is 243 meters high, with a 3,200 ton lifting capacity, making it one of the largest mobile cranes ever built.

PEGA.name: Pegasystems Inc.
PEGA.fact: Pegasystems has three regional HQs in North America, Europe, and Asia, with approximately 6,500 global employees.

THG.name: The Hanover Insurance Group, Inc.
THG.fact: This insurance company's deep historical roots date all the way back to 1852. Hanover Insurance prides itself on having paid cash dividends to its shareholders every year since 1853.

GWRE.name: Guidewire Software, Inc.
GWRE.fact: In 2015 and 2016, Guidewire was listed on the "Top 50 Large Companies" in Glassdoor's Best Places To Work.

INTU.name: Intuit Inc.
INTU.fact: Intuit employees get free pet insurance.

KYMR.name: Kymera Therapeutics, Inc.
KYMR.fact: Kymera is a clinical stage biotech focused on "targeted protein degradtion" (TPD), as a means to treat presently undruggable diseases. Much of its pipeline targets immuno-inflammatory diseases and liquid and solid state tumors.

TSCO.name: Tractor Supply Company
TSCO.fact: Tractor Supply Company is the largest operator of rural lifestyle retail stores in America.

LH.name: Labcorp Holdings Inc.
LH.fact: LabCorp typically processes tests on more than 2.5 million patient specimens per week.

AON.name: Aon plc
AON.fact: Aon is ranked 243rd in the Forbes Best Employers for New Grads list as of 2020.

PLUG.name: Plug Power Inc.
PLUG.fact: Plug Power Inc. specializes in hydrogen fuel cell technology. Hydrogen fuel cells use an electrochemical reaction to provide zero-emission energy that can be used to power anything from commercial vehicles to data centers to drones. Amazon was an early investor.

FRO.name: Frontline Plc
FRO.fact: Frontline operates a global fleet of some of the world's largest ships, including Suezmax, Aframax, and VLCC vessels. Several exceed 300,000 metric tons.

PEN.name: Penumbra, Inc.
PEN.fact: Helping patients needing treatment for strokes and aneurisms, Penumbra offers sophisticated and innovative Neuro and Vascular devices.

EQIX.name: Equinix, Inc.
EQIX.fact: Equinix's Frankfurt facilities are an established European gateway to global trading opportunities, financial services and trading venues. In Frankfurt, Equinix customers get access to a multi-asset/multi-venue financial service ecosystem, benefitting from low latency connections to other market participants.

OCUL.name: Ocular Therapeutix, Inc.
